definition_zh: 计划；节目；计算机程序；为……编写程序
definition_en: a written plan of action, a list or show, or a set of coded instructions; to arrange or write such instructions
core_image: 墙上贴着一张写满时间与步骤的纸，旁边的旧机器照着纸条上的指令一行行运行
scene: 工作室的墙上贴着一张写满时间与步骤的纸，旁边的旧机器正照着纸条上的指令一行行运行。The engineer loaded the program and watched the machine follow each line.
sceneCN: 这里 program 指交给计算机执行的一整套指令（第 4 个义项：计算机程序）；句意：工程师载入程序，看着机器逐行执行。图中可辨识物件：墙上的时间表、纸条、旧机器、指示灯。

derivatives.zh: 纲领性的；按计划行事的

senses.title: A plan of future action
senses.definition: a set of intended actions arranged in advance to reach a goal
senses.definitionCN: 为了达到某个目标而事先安排好的一系列行动
senses.example: The city launched a housing program for low-income families.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府启动了一项面向低收入家庭的住房计划。
senses.why: the Greek noun began as a public notice written down ahead of time, so the word still carries the idea of something laid out before it happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊名词最初指事先写好的公开通告，因此这个词始终带着「事情发生之前就摆好的安排」这一层意思。

senses.title: An order of events
senses.definition: a list showing the times and order of the parts of an event
senses.definitionCN: 列出活动各部分时间与顺序的清单
senses.example: The conference program lists every talk and the room it uses.
senses.exampleCN: 会议日程列出了每场报告及其所在房间。
senses.why: a written notice of what will happen and when is the most literal survival of the original sense.
senses.whyCN: 把「将发生什么、何时发生」写下来通告，正是原义最直接的延续。

senses.title: A printed list for an audience
senses.definition: the printed sheet given to an audience, naming the performers and the works
senses.definitionCN: 发给观众、写明演出者与曲目的印刷纸页
senses.example: She read the program before the orchestra tuned up.
senses.exampleCN: 乐团调音之前，她先读了节目单。
senses.why: theatres turned the order of a performance into a small printed booklet, and the booklet took the name of the order itself.
senses.whyCN: 剧院把演出顺序做成一本小册子，册子便直接沿用了「顺序」这个名字。

senses.title: A show that is broadcast
senses.definition: a single show or an ongoing series carried by a station
senses.definitionCN: 由电台或电视台播出的单个节目或系列节目
senses.example: The station dropped the program after one season.
senses.exampleCN: 电视台播出一季后停掉了这个节目。
senses.why: broadcasting inherited the word from theatre: each slot in the schedule is a program, whether or not paper is involved.
senses.whyCN: 广播沿用了剧院的说法：节目表上的每一个时段都叫一个节目，与纸张已无关系。

senses.title: Instructions a computer follows
senses.definition: an ordered set of coded instructions that makes a computer carry out a task
senses.definitionCN: 使计算机完成一项任务的有序编码指令集合
senses.example: The program sorts the files by date and deletes the copies.
senses.exampleCN: 这个程序按日期排序文件并删除重复副本。
senses.why: the earliest electronic machines were fed a written sequence of steps, exactly like a plan handed to a reader, so the plan word moved onto the machine.
senses.whyCN: 最早的电子机器接收的是一份写好的步骤序列，就像交给读者的一份计划，于是「计划」这个词就移到了机器上。

senses.title: A course of study
senses.definition: an organized course or set of courses leading to a qualification
senses.definitionCN: 通向某种资格的有组织课程或课程组合
senses.example: The new program leads to a master's degree in two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新课程两年后可获硕士学位。
senses.why: schools borrowed the plan word because a degree is also a sequence of steps that a student is expected to complete in order.
senses.whyCN: 学校借用了「计划」这个词，因为拿学位同样是一串要求学生按顺序完成的步骤。

senses.title: A government or agency scheme
senses.definition: an official scheme that organizes money and staff for a public purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为公共目的组织资金与人员的官方方案
senses.example: The literacy program trained teachers in three rural counties.
senses.exampleCN: 这项扫盲计划在三个农村县培训了教师。
senses.why: public bodies write down what they intend to do and fund it, and that funded intention is called a program.
senses.whyCN: 公共机构把打算做的事写下来并拨款，这份带钱的打算就被称为项目。

senses.title: To set something to happen
senses.definition: to arrange for a device or system to act at a set time or in a set way
senses.definitionCN: 安排某个设备或系统在固定时间或以固定方式动作
senses.example: They programmed the lights to switch off at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把灯设定在午夜自动关闭。
senses.why: once a machine can hold its own sequence of steps, the verb means putting that sequence into it, even when no code is written by hand.
senses.whyCN: 一旦机器能自己保存步骤序列，动词就表示把序列装进去，哪怕并没有手写代码。

senses.title: To write instructions for a machine
senses.definition: to write the code that a computer or machine will execute
senses.definitionCN: 编写计算机或机器将要执行的代码
senses.example: He programmed the robot to pick only the ripe fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 他给机器人编程，让它只摘成熟的果子。
senses.why: this is the modern verb built directly on the computing noun: the programmer writes the plan the machine will follow.
senses.whyCN: 这是直接由计算机义名词转来的现代动词：程序员写下机器将要遵循的计划。

intro.en: Program is Greek in origin, Latin in transmission and French in form. Its oldest sense is a public notice written in advance; the computing sense is a twentieth-century extension. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: program 源于希腊语，经拉丁语传递，形式取自法语。它最古老的意思是事先写好的公开通告；计算机义是二十世纪的延伸。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek programma meant a public written notice, built from pro-, before, and graphein, to write. The noun named a posted announcement, not a scheme of action.
items.cn: 希腊语 programma 指公开的书面通告，由 pro-「在前」与 graphein「书写」构成。这个名词指的是张贴出来的公告，而不是行动计划。

items.en: Latin borrowed programma as a learned noun for a written notice or preface, keeping the Greek shape and the written, public flavour.
items.cn: 拉丁语借用 programma 作为书面通告或序言的学术名词，保留了希腊语的形式与「书面、公开」的色彩。

items.en: French programme entered English in the seventeenth century. English first used it for a public notice and soon for the printed order of a ceremony or performance.
items.cn: 法语 programme 在十七世纪进入英语。英语先用它指公开通告，很快又用它指仪式或演出的印刷顺序。

items.en: American printers shortened the ending to program. The two spellings now divide mainly by region, and the short form became standard in computing.
items.cn: 美国印刷者把词尾缩短为 program。两种拼写如今基本按地区分工，而短形式在计算机领域成为标准。

items.en: From the 1940s a program meant the coded sequence that drives a machine. The noun, and then the verb to program, followed the hardware into ordinary use.
items.cn: 自 1940 年代起，program 指驱动机器的编码序列。名词以及后来的动词「编程」随硬件一起进入日常使用。

items.en: The chain from Greek programma through Latin programma and French programme to English program is documented. Only the first written dates in English are approximate, and any Indo-European root proposed for graphein is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：从希腊语 programma 经拉丁语 programma、法语 programme 到英语的这条链有文献依据，只是英语最早书证的年代为约数；为 graphein 提出的印欧语词根属于重构形式，并非有记录的词。

note.en: The first group is the same word in other shapes and roles; the second group names neighbouring ideas of a plan, a timetable and software.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的其他形式与角色；第二组是与计划、时间表和软件相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same noun, and the usual form for a printed list of performances; computing writing prefers program everywhere.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个名词的英式拼写，也是节目单的常用形式；计算机写作各地多用 program。

entries.definition: The activity of writing code, not the code of one task; the noun names the work, while program names the product.
entries.definitionCN: 指编写代码这项活动，而不是某一任务的代码；名词指工作，program 指成品。

entries.definition: The person who writes the code; it answers who, where program answers what.
entries.definitionCN: 指写代码的人；它回答「谁」，而 program 回答「什么」。

entries.definition: Built on the Greek noun with a Latinised ending: it describes something done by fixed plan, as in programmatic music or programmatic reform.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊名词加拉丁化词尾构成：描述按固定计划进行的事物，如标题音乐或按纲领推行的改革。

entries.definition: The broad intention and the steps meant to reach it; a program is usually a plan that has been written down, funded or scheduled.
entries.definitionCN: 指总体意图及实现它的步骤；program 通常是已写下来、已拨款或已排期的计划。

entries.definition: The arrangement of times and dates; a program may contain a schedule, but a schedule says only when, not what for.
entries.definitionCN: 指时间与日期的安排；program 里可能含 schedule，但时间表只说「何时」，不说「为何」。

entries.definition: Programs and data treated as a product or a body of material; one program is a single unit of software.
entries.definitionCN: 把程序与数据当作产品与整套材料；一个 program 是软件的一个单元。

entries.definition: The list of items to be discussed at a meeting; it is a program for a discussion rather than for a machine or a season.
entries.definitionCN: 会议上要讨论的事项清单；它是讨论的程序，而非机器或演出季的程序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek pieces, the real family and the real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊语构件、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek pro- means before and graphein means write, so a program is something written down before it happens.
normal.cn: 希腊语 pro- 意为「在前」，graphein 意为「书写」，所以 program 就是事先写下来的东西。

normal.en: The family runs program, programme, programming, programmer, programmable and programmatic.
normal.cn: 同族词有 program、programme、programming、programmer、programmable 与 programmatic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the plan sense: training program, welfare program, housing program.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示「计划」义：培训计划、福利计划、住房计划。

normal.en: The two spellings differ only in the ending, and computing settles on program everywhere.
normal.cn: 两种拼写只差词尾，计算机领域各地都落在 program 上。

normal.en: The verb splits by object: you program a computer with code, and you program a timer with a setting.
normal.cn: 动词按宾语分工：给计算机编程是写代码，给定时器设程序是调设定。

abstract.en: Picture a playbill that keeps fluttering after the audience has gone, still deciding the order of a night that is over.
abstract.cn: 想象一张观众散场后仍在飘动的节目单，还在决定一个已经结束的夜晚的顺序。

abstract.en: Picture a strip of paper sliding into a machine, and the machine growing a spine as it reads.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸条滑进机器，机器一边读一边长出脊骨。

abstract.en: Picture traffic lights blinking to a timetable nobody in the street can see.
abstract.cn: 想象街上的红绿灯按一张路人看不见的时间表眨眼。

examples.en: A well-written program can be read by another person without running it.
examples.cn: 写得好的程序，别人不运行也能读懂。

examples.en: The museum program lists four lectures and one concert.
examples.cn: 博物馆的活动日程列出四场讲座和一场音乐会。

examples.en: She programmed the irrigation system to water the field before dawn.
examples.cn: 她把灌溉系统设定在黎明前浇水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑（pro）来个（gram）」——事先扑上去写下来的东西，就是计划与程序

root: 希腊 pro-「在前」+ graphein「书写」→ programma「公开书面通告」→ 拉丁 programma → 法语 programme → 英语 program；计算机义始于二十世纪四十年代。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one thread: something is written down in advance, first as a notice, then as an order of events, a printed list, a show, a set of machine instructions, a course, a funded scheme, and at last as the act of setting or coding.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一条线索展开：某事被事先写下来，先是通告，再是活动顺序、印刷节目单、播出节目、机器指令集、课程、拨款项目，最后是设定与编程这两个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet of times and steps pinned to the wall, with a machine reading the sheet line by line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写满时间与步骤的纸钉在墙上，机器一行行读着这张纸。

branches.en: PLAN AND SCHEME: an intention set down in advance, whether a household plan or a funded public scheme.
branches.cn: 计划与方案：事先写下的意图，无论家务安排还是拨款推行的公共项目。

branches.en: TIME ARRANGEMENT: an order of events in time, applied to people and then to devices that must act on cue.
branches.cn: 时间安排：按时间排出的活动顺序，先用于人，后用于必须按时动作的设备。

branches.en: LIST AND SHOW: the printed order becomes a booklet, and the booklet gives its name to the broadcast item.
branches.cn: 节目单与节目：印刷的顺序成为小册子，小册子又把名字让给播出的节目。

branches.en: CODE: the written sequence is now for a machine, first as a noun and then as the verb that puts it there.
branches.cn: 代码：写下的序列改为给机器用，先是名词，再是把序列装进去的动词。

branches.en: COURSE OF STUDY: a degree is also a sequence of steps completed in order, so schools use the same word.
branches.cn: 课程：学位同样是一串按顺序完成的步骤，学校于是沿用同一个词。

intro.en: Program is Greek in its two pieces, Latin in its noun ending and French in its modern shape. English then added -ing, -er and -able to build the computing family.
intro.cn: program 的两个构件来自希腊语，名词词尾来自拉丁语，现代形式来自法语。英语随后加 -ing、-er、-able 构成计算机词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin programma is the one learned borrowing that carries the word from Greek into French and English; the other Latin-looking ending -atic came later through French adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 programma 是把这个词从希腊语带到法语与英语的唯一学术借词；另一个似拉丁的词尾 -atic 是后来经法语形容词进入的。

items.example: The prefix places the writing ahead of the event.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「写」放在事情发生之前。

items.example: The verb names the act of setting marks down.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把符号落下来的动作。

items.example: The ending turns the act of writing into a written thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把「写」这个动作变成「写出来的东西」。

items.example: The Greek noun is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词是整个词族的源头。

items.meaning: a notice; an order of events
items.example: English took the French shape in the seventeenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语在十七世纪接受了法语的形式。

items.meaning: a plan or a coded instruction set
items.example: The short spelling became standard in computing.
items.exampleCN: 短拼写在计算机领域成为标准。

items.example: Programming names the work rather than the product.
items.exampleCN: programming 指这项工作，而不是成品。

items.example: A programmer is the one who writes the code.
items.exampleCN: programmer 就是写代码的人。

items.example: A programmable device can hold a new sequence.
items.exampleCN: 可编程设备能装入新的序列。

items.example: Programmatic music follows a written story.
items.exampleCN: 标题音乐遵循一个写好的故事。

definition_zh: 编程；程序设计；程序（总称）；活动编排
definition_en: the activity or skill of writing computer programs, the programs so written, or the arranging of a schedule
core_image: 深夜的桌上摊着写满符号的笔记，屏幕上的光标一格一格往下走
scene: 深夜的桌上摊着写满符号的笔记，屏幕上的光标一格一格往下走，旁边的测试窗口不断刷新。She learned programming by rewriting small examples until they worked.
sceneCN: 这里 programming 指编写计算机程序这件事（第 1 个义项：编写程序的活动与技能）；句意：她通过反复改写小例子直到它们能运行来学习编程。图中可辨识物件：笔记、屏幕、光标、测试窗口。

pos.zh: 编程；程序设计；节目编排

senses.title: Writing code as an activity
senses.definition: the work of writing, testing and correcting the instructions a computer runs
senses.definitionCN: 编写、测试与修正计算机所执行指令的工作
senses.example: Programming takes patience as much as mathematical skill.
senses.exampleCN: 编程需要的耐心不亚于数学能力。
senses.why: the gerund turns the product into a process, so the word names the doing rather than the finished code.
senses.whyCN: 动名词把成品变成过程，因此这个词命名的是「做」这件事，而不是写好的代码。

senses.title: The code already written
senses.definition: the programs held by a machine or a system, taken as a body of code
senses.definitionCN: 机器或系统里所存程序的总和，被当作一整套代码
senses.example: The programming on that old machine is out of date.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧机器里的程序已经过时了。
senses.why: English often uses a gerund for a collective product, as in clothing or building, and code stored in a device is treated the same way.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用动名词指集合性的产物，如衣物、建筑，存放在设备里的代码也这样处理。

senses.title: The field of study
senses.definition: the discipline taught in schools and researched as a subject in its own right
senses.definitionCN: 在学校教授、并作为独立学科被研究的领域
senses.example: She teaches programming to first-year engineering students.
senses.exampleCN: 她给一年级工科学生教编程。
senses.why: once the activity acquired methods and a body of theory, the gerund became the name of a school subject.
senses.whyCN: 当这项活动有了方法与理论体系，动名词就成了课程名称。

senses.title: Arranging a schedule of events
senses.definition: the planning work that decides which events happen and in what order
senses.definitionCN: 决定哪些活动举行、按什么顺序进行的设计工作
senses.example: Festival programming begins a full year before the first concert.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐节的节目编排在第一场音乐会前整整一年就开始了。
senses.why: this is the older, non-computing sense: a person programs a season by deciding its order, without any machine involved.
senses.whyCN: 这是更早的非计算机义：人通过决定顺序来编排一个演出季，完全不涉及机器。

senses.title: Planning what a channel airs
senses.definition: the work of choosing and ordering the shows a station broadcasts
senses.definitionCN: 挑选并安排电台或电视台播出节目的工作
senses.example: Channel programming now reacts to what viewers watch live.
senses.exampleCN: 频道编排如今会随观众实时观看的情况调整。
senses.why: broadcasting kept the scheduling sense and gave it a permanent home in the industry.
senses.whyCN: 广播保留了「排顺序」这层意思，并让它在行业里安了家。

senses.title: Setting a device's timed actions
senses.definition: entering times and conditions so that a device acts automatically
senses.definitionCN: 输入时间与条件，使设备自动动作
senses.example: The programming of the heating system took only a few minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 给供暖系统做设定只花了几分钟。
senses.why: a timer also holds a small plan, so the gerund covers the act of loading that plan.
senses.whyCN: 定时器也存着一份小计划，因此动名词也涵盖装入这份计划的动作。

senses.title: Instructing a non-computer machine
senses.definition: writing the control sequence for a robot, a lathe or other industrial machine
senses.definitionCN: 为机器人、车床或其他工业机器编写控制序列
senses.example: Robot programming now uses visual blocks instead of typed lines.
senses.exampleCN: 机器人编程如今用可视化积木而不是敲代码行。
senses.why: the machine does not need to be a general computer for the same word to apply, as long as it follows a written sequence.
senses.whyCN: 机器不必是通用计算机，只要它遵循写好的序列，同一个词就照样适用。

senses.title: Behaviour built into a device
senses.definition: the fixed sequence of responses designed into a product
senses.definitionCN: 产品中被设计好的固定反应序列
senses.example: The toy's programming makes it sing whenever it is shaken.
senses.exampleCN: 这个玩具的内置程序使它一被摇动就唱歌。
senses.why: when the sequence is sealed inside a product, the gerund names the behaviour rather than the writing of it.
senses.whyCN: 当序列被封在产品内部，动名词指的就是行为本身，而不是编写它的过程。

intro.en: Programming is English through and through: the Greek-derived noun program plus the English gerund ending -ing. Its scheduling sense is older than its computing sense. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: programming 是地道的英语构词：希腊来源的名词 program 加英语动名词词尾 -ing。它的「排日程」义比计算机义更早。年代均为约数。

items.en: The base noun program goes back to Greek programma, a public written notice built from pro-, before, and graphein, to write.
items.cn: 基础名词 program 可追到希腊语 programma「公开书面通告」，由 pro-「在前」与 graphein「书写」构成。

items.en: The ending -ing is native English: it turns a verb into the name of its activity, and it has done so since Old English.
items.cn: 词尾 -ing 是英语本族语素：它把动词变成该活动的名称，这一用法自上古英语时期就有。

items.en: In the nineteenth century programming meant drawing up the programme of a concert, a season or a course, with no reference to machinery.
items.cn: 十九世纪时 programming 指排定音乐会、演出季或课程的节目顺序，与机器无关。

items.en: From the 1940s and 1950s the same gerund named the new work of preparing instructions for an electronic computer, and that sense soon dominated.
items.cn: 自 1940 至 1950 年代，同一个动名词开始指为电子计算机准备指令的新工作，这一义很快占了主导。

items.en: Radio and television kept the older scheduling sense alive: programming is what a channel planner does, distinct from writing software.
items.cn: 广播与电视让较早的「排顺序」义活了下来：programming 是频道编排者做的事，与写软件不同。

items.en: The base noun and the native gerund ending are both documented, and the formation is transparent. Only the earliest recorded dates of the scheduling and computing senses are approximate, and any deeper Indo-European root for graphein is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：基础名词与英语本族动名词词尾都有文献依据，构词关系清楚；只是「排日程」义与计算机义的最早记录年代为约数，为 graphein 提出的更早印欧语词根属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is the same stem in its other roles; the second group names the neighbouring activities of coding, building software and scheduling.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词干的其他角色；第二组是与写代码、做软件、排日程相邻的说法。

entries.definition: One finished set of instructions, or the plan behind it; programming is the work that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 指一套写好的指令或背后的计划；programming 是产出它的工作。

entries.definition: The person doing the work; it is the agent noun built with -er on the same base.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事这项工作的人；它是同一词干加 -er 构成的施事名词。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the noun, and the usual word for the printed order of a performance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词的英式拼写，也常指演出的印刷节目单。

entries.definition: Able to receive and hold a new sequence; it describes a capacity, not the work of writing the sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 指能够接收并保存新序列；它描述能力，不指编写序列的工作。

entries.definition: The hands-on writing of code, often used for the practical side; programming also covers design, testing and reasoning.
entries.definitionCN: 指动手写代码，常指实务那面；programming 还包括设计、测试与推理。

entries.definition: The whole process of building software, including requirements, design, testing and maintenance; programming is its central craft.
entries.definitionCN: 指构建软件的全过程，含需求、设计、测试与维护；programming 是其中的核心手艺。

entries.definition: Writing short programs that automate a task, usually in an interpreted language; narrower and more task-bound than programming.
entries.definitionCN: 指编写自动完成某任务的短程序，多用于解释型语言；比 programming 更窄、更贴任务。

entries.definition: Arranging times and dates; it overlaps with the older sense of programming but says nothing about content or code.
entries.definitionCN: 指安排时间与日期；与 programming 较早的词义有交集，但不涉及内容或代码。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real base noun, the real ending and the real phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的基础名词、真实的词尾与真实的搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Program plus -ing: the ending turns the product into the ongoing work.
normal.cn: program 加 -ing：词尾把成品变成正在进行的工作。

normal.en: The family runs program, programming, programmer, programmable and reprogram.
normal.cn: 同族词有 program、programming、programmer、programmable 与 reprogram。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the computing sense: programming language, pair programming, programming model.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出计算机义：编程语言、结对编程、编程模型。

normal.en: The same word still means arranging a festival or a channel, which is why a concert hall can have a programmer too.
normal.cn: 这个词仍指编排音乐节或频道，所以音乐厅也会有节目编排者。

normal.en: A gerund can name a body of material, so the code stored in a machine is simply its programming.
normal.cn: 动名词可以指一整套材料，所以机器里存的代码就叫它的程序。

abstract.en: Picture a note that keeps being rewritten while the machine reads it aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象一张笔记，机器一边朗读，它一边被改写。

abstract.en: Picture a garden whose planting order is decided years before the first seed.
abstract.cn: 想象一座花园，播种顺序在第一粒种子之前几年就定好了。

abstract.en: Picture a thermostat humming a small tune it was taught once and never forgets.
abstract.cn: 想象一台恒温器哼着一支被教会一次就再没忘记的小调。

examples.en: Programming is now taught alongside mathematics in many schools.
examples.cn: 如今许多学校把编程与数学一起教。

examples.en: The programming in this device cannot be changed by the user.
examples.cn: 这台设备里的程序用户无法更改。

examples.en: Her festival programming put new composers beside old ones.
examples.cn: 她的音乐节编排把新作曲家与老作曲家放在一起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑（pro）来（gram）明（ming）」——事先把步骤写明白，就是编程

root: 希腊 pro-「在前」+ graphein「书写」→ programma → 法语 programme → 英语 program；再加英语动名词词尾 -ing 构成 programming。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split into two eras: first the arranging of events, then the writing, storing, teaching, setting and embedding of machine instructions.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分属两个时期：先是对活动的编排，后是对机器指令的编写、存储、教学、设定与内置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a written sequence of steps, either held by a planner or loaded into a machine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份写好的步骤序列，或握在编排者手里，或被装进机器。

branches.en: WORK AND PRODUCT: the same gerund names the doing and the code that results from it.
branches.cn: 工作与成品：同一个动名词既指「做」，也指由此产生的代码。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE: methods and theory turn the activity into a taught subject.
branches.cn: 学科：方法与理论把这项活动变成可教的科目。

branches.en: SCHEDULING: a festival and a channel are both programmed by deciding order, with no machine in sight.
branches.cn: 排期：音乐节与频道都靠决定顺序来编排，完全不涉及机器。

branches.en: SETTING MACHINES: the sequence is entered into a timer, a robot or a lathe, none of which is a general computer.
branches.cn: 设定机器：序列被输入定时器、机器人或车床，它们都不是通用计算机。

branches.en: BUILT-IN BEHAVIOUR: once sealed inside a product, the sequence is the behaviour itself.
branches.cn: 内置行为：序列一旦封进产品，它就是行为本身。

intro.en: The word is a Greek-derived noun wearing a native English ending: programma supplies the base, -ing supplies the sense of ongoing activity.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊来源的名词戴着英语本族词尾：programma 提供词干，-ing 提供「持续活动」的意思。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes only programma, the learned noun that reached English through French; the working parts of programming itself are Greek and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只贡献了 programma 这个经法语进入英语的学术名词；programming 本身的构件则来自希腊语与英语。

items.example: The base noun supplies the written-plan image.
items.exampleCN: 基础名词提供了「书面计划」的意象。

items.example: The verb is the oldest layer of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族里最老的一层。

items.meaning: a plan; a set of instructions
items.example: The noun is the base of the gerund.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是动名词的词基。

items.example: The ending makes the product into a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把成品变成过程。

items.example: Programming became a school subject in the twentieth century.
items.exampleCN: programming 在二十世纪成了学校科目。

items.example: The agent noun programmer comes from the same base.
items.exampleCN: 施事名词 programmer 出自同一词基。

items.example: Programmable devices accept a new sequence.
items.exampleCN: 可编程设备接受新序列。

items.example: To reprogram is to load a sequence again.
items.exampleCN: reprogram 就是重新装入序列。

items.example: The programmer and the programming share one base.
items.exampleCN: programmer 与 programming 共享一个词基。

items.example: The adjective belongs to the older planning sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词属于较早的「计划」义。

definition_zh: 程序员；程序编制者；节目编排者
definition_en: a person who writes computer programs, or one who plans the order of events or broadcasts
core_image: 办公室一角，一个人盯着屏幕上滚动的报错，手指停在键盘上
scene: 办公室的一角，一个人盯着屏幕上滚动的报错，手指停在键盘上，桌上放着一杯凉掉的茶。The programmer traced the fault to a single line of code.
sceneCN: 这里 programmer 指编写计算机程序的人（第 1 个义项：编写程序的人）；句意：这位程序员把故障追到一行代码上。图中可辨识物件：屏幕、报错行、键盘、凉茶。

pos.zh: 程序员；程序编制者；节目编排者

derivatives.zh: 纲领性的；按计划行事的

senses.title: A person who writes code
senses.definition: someone whose work is to write and correct the instructions a computer runs
senses.definitionCN: 以编写与修正计算机所执行指令为工作的人
senses.example: The programmer traced the fault to a single line of code.
senses.exampleCN: 这位程序员把故障追到一行代码上。
senses.why: the agent ending -er on the base program gives the plainest sense: the one who writes the program.
senses.whyCN: 词基 program 加施事词尾 -er，最直接的意思就是写程序的人。

senses.title: A software professional
senses.definition: a job title for someone employed to build and maintain software in a team
senses.definitionCN: 在团队中被雇来构建与维护软件的职业头衔
senses.example: The company hired ten programmers for the new app.
senses.exampleCN: 公司为这款新应用雇了十名程序员。
senses.why: the craft became an industry job, and the simple agent noun became a payroll category.
senses.whyCN: 这门手艺成了行业岗位，简单的施事名词也成了工资表上的类别。

senses.title: One who plans an event programme
senses.definition: the person who decides which acts, films or talks appear and in what order
senses.definitionCN: 决定哪些节目、影片或报告出现及其顺序的人
senses.example: The festival programmer chose films from thirty countries.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐节的节目编排者选了三十个国家的影片。
senses.why: this is the older sense: a programmer programs a season by deciding its running order, with no computer involved.
senses.whyCN: 这是较早的词义：编排者通过决定演出顺序来编排一个演出季，不涉及计算机。

senses.title: One who sets a device
senses.definition: a person who enters times and conditions into a timer or control unit
senses.definitionCN: 把时间与条件输入定时器或控制单元的人
senses.example: The heating programmer came to set the boiler for winter.
senses.exampleCN: 供暖设定员来把锅炉调成冬季模式。
senses.why: when the task is only to load a small sequence into a household device, the agent noun still fits.
senses.whyCN: 当任务只是往家用设备里装入一小段序列时，这个施事名词依然适用。

senses.title: A channel schedule planner
senses.definition: a broadcast professional who chooses what a station airs and when
senses.definitionCN: 决定电台或电视台播什么、何时播的广播从业者
senses.example: As a channel programmer, she decides what airs on Fridays.
senses.exampleCN: 作为频道编排者，她决定周五播什么。
senses.why: broadcasting kept the scheduling sense and turned it into a distinct job title.
senses.whyCN: 广播保留了「排顺序」义，并把它变成一个独立职位。

senses.title: A systems-level specialist
senses.definition: someone who works close to the operating system, drivers or hardware interfaces
senses.definitionCN: 在操作系统、驱动或硬件接口附近工作的人
senses.example: The systems programmer rewrote the device driver in assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 系统程序员用汇编重写了设备驱动。
senses.why: once software split into layers, the same title gained a prefix that marks how deep the work goes.
senses.whyCN: 软件一旦分层，同一个头衔就加上前缀，标明工作深入到哪一层。

senses.title: One who programs industrial machines
senses.definition: a technician who writes control sequences for machine tools or production equipment
senses.definitionCN: 为机床或生产设备编写控制序列的技术人员
senses.example: The shop hired a control programmer for its new lathe.
senses.exampleCN: 车间为新机床雇了一名控制编程员。
senses.why: the machine need not be a computer; a written sequence of movements is enough to make the title apply.
senses.whyCN: 机器不必是计算机，只要有一份写好的动作序列，这个头衔就成立。

senses.title: A statistical programmer
senses.definition: a specialist who writes analysis code for clinical trials or large studies
senses.definitionCN: 为临床试验或大型研究编写分析代码的专职人员
senses.example: The statistical programmer prepared the tables for the trial report.
senses.exampleCN: 统计程序员为试验报告准备了表格。
senses.why: fields that depend on repeated analysis gave the general title a domain adjective and a fixed role.
senses.whyCN: 依赖重复分析的领域给这个通用头衔加上领域形容词，形成固定岗位。

intro.en: Programmer is program plus the native agent ending -er. Its event-planning sense is nineteenth-century; the computing sense arrived with electronic machines in the 1940s. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: programmer 是 program 加英语本族施事词尾 -er。它的「编排活动」义产生于十九世纪；计算机义随电子机器在 1940 年代到来。年代均为约数。

items.en: The base noun descends from Greek programma, a written public notice, through Latin programma and French programme.
items.cn: 基础名词经拉丁语 programma 与法语 programme，源自希腊语 programma「公开书面通告」。

items.en: The ending -er is native English and marks the doer of an action; its use here is no different from writer or builder.
items.cn: 词尾 -er 是英语本族语素，标记动作的执行者；这里的用法与 writer、builder 并无不同。

items.en: A programmer first meant a person who arranged the programme of a concert or a ceremony, and the word is recorded in that sense before computing existed.
items.cn: programmer 最初指安排音乐会或仪式节目顺序的人，这一义在计算机出现之前已有记录。

items.en: In the 1940s the operators who prepared instruction sequences for electronic computers were called programmers, and the title spread with the industry.
items.cn: 1940 年代，为电子计算机准备指令序列的操作者被称为 programmer，这一头衔随产业扩散。

items.en: Later prefixes such as systems, applications and statistical split the one craft into named roles without changing the base meaning.
items.cn: 后来系统、应用、统计等前缀把这门手艺分成具名岗位，但基础含义未变。

items.en: The base noun plus the native agent ending is a transparent English formation recorded from the nineteenth century. Only the earliest dates of the two senses are approximate, and any deeper Indo-European root for graphein is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：基础名词加英语本族施事词尾，是构词清楚的英语形式，十九世纪已有书证；只是两个义项的最早年代为约数，为 graphein 提出的更早印欧语词根属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is the same stem with other endings; the second group names neighbouring software roles and the older event planner.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词干加不同词尾；第二组是与软件岗位相邻的职业，以及较早的活动编排者。

entries.definition: The instructions themselves; a programmer produces a program, so the two differ as doer and product.
entries.definitionCN: 指指令本身；程序员产出程序，二者是「做的人」与「成品」的关系。

entries.definition: The work the programmer does; the person and the activity share one base and differ only in ending.
entries.definitionCN: 指程序员所做的工作；人与活动共享一个词基，只差词尾。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the product noun, especially the printed order of a performance.
entries.definitionCN: 成品名词的英式拼写，尤指演出的印刷节目单。

entries.definition: Able to take a new sequence; it describes the equipment a programmer works on, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 指能装入新序列；它描述程序员操作的设备，而不是人。

entries.definition: A broader software role that also covers design, requirements and release work; a programmer may be one part of that role.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽的软件岗位，还涵盖设计、需求与发布；程序员可能只是其中一部分。

entries.definition: An informal word for someone who writes code, often implying craft without design responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 写代码者的口语说法，常暗示只管实现、不管设计。

entries.definition: A title stressing systematic design and standards; software engineer is often the formal version of programmer.
entries.definitionCN: 强调系统设计与规范的职称；软件工程师常是程序员的正式说法。

entries.definition: The person who selects and arranges a programme of works or events; close to the older sense of programmer, but with an emphasis on care and selection.
entries.definitionCN: 挑选并安排作品或活动顺序的人；接近 programmer 的较早词义，但更强调挑选与照管。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real base noun, the real agent ending and the real job titles, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的基础名词、真实的施事词尾与真实职位名，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Program plus -er: the ending marks the person, so programmer is the one who writes the program.
normal.cn: program 加 -er：词尾标记人，所以 programmer 就是写程序的人。

normal.en: The family runs programmer, programming, program, programmable and reprogram.
normal.cn: 同族词有 programmer、programming、program、programmable 与 reprogram。

normal.en: Job titles mark the specialities: systems programmer, application programmer, statistical programmer.
normal.cn: 职位名标出专长：系统程序员、应用开发程序员、统计程序员。

normal.en: The older sense survives in arts administration, where a festival programmer arranges the season.
normal.cn: 较早的词义仍在艺术管理里存活：音乐节的节目编排者安排整个演出季。

normal.en: A programmer works on a program, and the two words differ only by the ending -er.
normal.cn: 程序员做的是程序，两个词只差词尾 -er。

abstract.en: Picture a person who reads a wall of errors the way a doctor reads a rash.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人读满屏报错，像医生看一片疹子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that stops mid-key because the next line would change everything.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手停在按键上方，因为下一行会改变一切。

abstract.en: Picture a playbill being rearranged by someone who will never meet the performers.
abstract.cn: 想象有人反复调整节目单，却永远不会见到台上的演员。

examples.en: A programmer often spends more time reading code than writing it.
examples.cn: 程序员读代码的时间往往比写代码多。

examples.en: The festival programmer placed the new work after the symphony.
examples.cn: 音乐节编排者把新作排在了交响曲之后。

examples.en: The statistical programmer checked every table before the report was filed.
examples.cn: 统计程序员在报告提交前核对了每张表。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑（pro）来（gram）马（mer）」——扑到键盘前写程序的那匹马，就是程序员

root: 希腊 programma「公开书面通告」→ 拉丁 programma → 法语 programme → 英语 program；加英语施事词尾 -er 构成 programmer。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses divide into two lives of one word: the computing craft with its specialities, and the older role of arranging an event or a broadcast.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分属这个词的两段生涯：计算机手艺及其细分岗位，以及较早的编排活动与播出内容的角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a keyboard, reading a wall of errors and writing the line that fixes them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人在键盘前读满屏报错，写下能修好它的那一行。

branches.en: CRAFT AND JOB: the person who writes code, and the same craft turned into a paid team role.
branches.cn: 手艺与职业：写代码的人，以及同一门手艺变成的受雇团队岗位。

branches.en: DEPTH: systems programming marks how close the work sits to the machine.
branches.cn: 深度：系统编程标出工作离机器有多近。

branches.en: DOMAIN: industrial control and statistics both add an adjective instead of inventing a new noun.
branches.cn: 领域：工业控制与统计都只加一个形容词，而不另造名词。

branches.en: EVENT ORDER: festivals and channels are programmed by people, long before code existed.
branches.cn: 活动顺序：音乐节与频道由人编排，远在代码出现之前。

branches.en: DEVICE SETTING: loading a small sequence into a household unit is the domestic echo of the craft.
branches.cn: 设备设定：往家用设备里装入小序列，是这门手艺在家庭里的回声。

intro.en: Programmer is a Greek-derived base wearing the native English agent ending -er, the same pattern as writer and builder.
intro.cn: programmer 是希腊来源的词基戴着英语本族施事词尾 -er，与 writer、builder 同一模式。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes the noun programma, which carried the word into French; the agent ending itself is English, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语贡献了名词 programma，把词带到法语；施事词尾本身是英语的，不是拉丁语。

definition_zh: 编程语言；程序设计语言
definition_en: a formal notation in which instructions for a computer are written
core_image: 白板上写满箭头与括号，两行不同风格的符号被圈起来作对比

pos.zh: 编程语言；程序设计语言

senses.title: A notation for computer instructions
senses.titleCN: 书写计算机指令的记号系统
senses.definition: a formal system of symbols and rules in which a person writes what a computer must do
senses.definitionCN: 由符号与规则构成、供人书写计算机须做什么的形式系统
senses.example: Every programming language must define both what is allowed and what it means.
senses.exampleCN: 每门编程语言都必须规定什么写法合法、以及它的含义。
senses.why: the phrase joins the activity of programming to the general word for a system of signs, so its core sense is simply the sign system used for that activity.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把「编程」这项活动与泛指符号系统的「语言」拼在一起，核心义就是这项活动所用的符号系统。

senses.title: A particular named language
senses.definition: one specific language such as a named language with its own compiler or interpreter
senses.definitionCN: 某门具体语言，如有自己编译器或解释器的具名语言
senses.example: The course teaches one programming language in depth rather than five in passing.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课深入教一门编程语言，而不是走马观花教五门。
senses.why: users usually mean a single product when they say a language, because each one has its own grammar and toolchain.
senses.whyCN: 使用者说「一门语言」时通常指单个成品，因为每门都有自己的语法与工具链。

senses.title: A family sharing a paradigm
senses.definition: a group of languages built on one style of organizing computation, such as the functional or object-oriented family
senses.definitionCN: 按同一种组织计算的方式构成的一组语言，如函数式或面向对象语族
senses.example: The functional programming language family treats functions as ordinary values.
senses.exampleCN: 函数式编程语族把函数当作普通值来对待。
senses.why: languages inherit features from one another, so the phrase also names a lineage rather than a single product.
senses.whyCN: 语言之间会相互继承特征，因此这个短语也指一条谱系，而非单个成品。

senses.title: Its grammar and meaning as a study
senses.titleCN: 作为研究对象的语法与语义
senses.definition: the formal grammar and semantics of such notation, studied as a mathematical object
senses.definitionCN: 这类记号系统的形式语法与语义，被当作数学对象来研究
senses.example: Programming language theory asks which programs can be proved correct.
senses.exampleCN: 编程语言理论研究哪些程序可以被证明正确。
senses.why: once the notation is written down precisely, it can be analysed like any formal system, and the phrase names that object of study.
senses.whyCN: 记号一旦被精确写下，就能像任何形式系统一样被分析，短语于是指这个研究对象。

senses.title: A low-level notation
senses.definition: a language whose operations map closely onto machine instructions, such as assembly
senses.definitionCN: 操作与机器指令紧密对应的语言，如汇编
senses.example: Assembly is a programming language, but a programmer rarely writes a whole system in it.
senses.exampleCN: 汇编是一门编程语言，但程序员很少用它写整个系统。
senses.why: the phrase covers depth as well as breadth: closeness to the hardware is a matter of degree, not of being a language or not.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语既涵盖广度也涵盖深度：离硬件近不近是程度问题，而不是算不算语言的问题。

senses.title: A high-level notation
senses.definition: a language whose statements are far from machine detail and closer to human reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 语句远离机器细节、更接近人的推理的语言
senses.example: A high-level programming language hides memory addresses behind named variables.
senses.exampleCN: 高级编程语言用具名变量把内存地址藏起来。
senses.why: the same phrase describes the opposite end of the scale, because what matters is that instructions are written in a notation at all.
senses.whyCN: 同一个短语也描述另一端，因为关键在于指令确实是用某种记号写成的。

senses.title: A notation for one narrow domain
senses.definition: a language designed for one problem area, such as querying data or typesetting
senses.definitionCN: 为某一问题领域设计的语言，如查询数据或排版
senses.example: A domain-specific programming language can be small and still be complete for its task.
senses.exampleCN: 领域特定的编程语言可以很小，却对其任务而言是完整的。
senses.why: narrowing the domain does not remove the language, it only limits what the notation must express.
senses.whyCN: 缩小领域并不取消「语言」的身份，只是限制了这套记号必须表达什么。

senses.title: A notation for controlling a machine
senses.definition: a language used to write movement or operation sequences for a device rather than a general computer
senses.definitionCN: 为设备而非通用计算机编写动作或操作序列的语言
senses.example: The lathe reads a programming language written as a list of tool movements.
senses.exampleCN: 车床读取一种写成刀具动作清单的编程语言。
senses.why: the phrase follows the word program wherever it goes, including machines that never run a general operating system.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语跟着 program 这个词走，包括那些从不运行通用操作系统的机器。

intro.en: The phrase is a twentieth-century compound of two older words: programming from Greek programma, and language from Latin lingua. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语是二十世纪由两个更老的词合成的复合词：programming 出自希腊语 programma，language 出自拉丁语 lingua。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin lingua meant tongue and then language. It passed through Old French langue into English language, keeping both the bodily and the abstract sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lingua 先指舌头，再指语言。它经古法语 langue 进入英语 language，同时保留身体义与抽象义。

items.en: The other half goes back to Greek programma, a written notice, built from pro-, before, and graphein, to write.
items.cn: 另一半可追到希腊语 programma「书面通告」，由 pro-「在前」与 graphein「书写」构成。

items.en: Programming named the act of writing machine instructions from the 1940s, giving the compound its first half.
items.cn: 自 1940 年代起，programming 指编写机器指令的行为，为复合词提供了前半。

items.en: The full phrase appears with the first stored-program machines, when people needed to distinguish the notation from the computer and from natural language.
items.cn: 完整短语随第一批存储程序机器出现，因为人们需要把这套记号与计算机本身、与自然语言区分开。

items.en: As languages multiplied, the phrase stayed general while names such as Fortran, Lisp and C filled in the particular.
items.cn: 语言一多，这个短语保持泛指，而 Fortran、Lisp、C 等专名承担具体指称。

items.en: Both halves are documented: the second from Latin lingua, the first from Greek programma. The first use of the full phrase is dated only approximately, and any older Indo-European source for lingua is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：两半都有文献依据，后半出自拉丁语 lingua，前半出自希腊语 programma；完整短语最早使用的年代只有约数，lingua 更早的印欧语来源属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is the two halves of the phrase and their near relatives; the second group names neighbouring notions of code, syntax and notation.
note.cn: 第一组是短语的两半及其近亲；第二组是与代码、语法、记号相邻的概念。

entries.definition: The activity of writing code; alone it names the work, while the full phrase names the notation used in it.
entries.definitionCN: 指编写代码的活动；单独用时指工作，完整短语指工作中使用的记号系统。

entries.definition: Any system of signs, including speech; the phrase narrows it to the signs a computer can execute.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何符号系统，包括口语；短语把它收窄为计算机能执行的符号。

entries.definition: The person who writes in the language; a language is the medium, a programmer is the user.
entries.definitionCN: 指用这门语言书写的人；语言是媒介，程序员是使用者。

entries.definition: A single body of instructions; a programming language is the notation that many such bodies are written in.
entries.definitionCN: 指一套指令；编程语言是许多这样的指令集所用的记号。

entries.definition: The text actually written; it is what a programming language produces, not the language itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指实际写出的文本；它是编程语言的产物，不是语言本身。

entries.definition: The rules that decide which strings are well formed; syntax is one part of a programming language, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 决定哪些字符串合法的规则；语法是编程语言的一部分，而非全部。

entries.definition: Any agreed system of symbols for writing something down; a programming language is a notation built for execution.
entries.definitionCN: 任何约定用来书写某物的符号系统；编程语言是为执行而建的记号系统。

entries.definition: A notation that labels the structure of a document rather than instructing a machine; often confused with programming languages.
entries.definitionCN: 标注文档结构的记号，而不是给机器下指令；常与编程语言混淆。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real halves, the real fixed phrases and the real distinctions, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的构件、真实的固定搭配与真实的分界，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Programming is the activity, language is the sign system: together they name the notation used to write code.
normal.cn: programming 是活动，language 是符号系统：合起来就是写代码所用的记号系统。

normal.en: The family runs program, programming, programmer, language and linguistic.
normal.cn: 同族词有 program、programming、programmer、language 与 linguistic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: high-level, low-level, general-purpose, domain-specific.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出谱系：高级、低级、通用、领域特定。

normal.en: Latin lingua gave language, and English kept both tongue and language in one word.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 lingua 给出 language，英语把「舌头」与「语言」留在了同一个词里。

normal.en: A markup language labels a document; a programming language tells a machine what to do.
normal.cn: 标记语言标注文档；编程语言告诉机器做什么。

abstract.en: Picture two chalk circles on a board, each holding a different dialect of the same intention.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上两个粉笔圈，各自装着同一种意图的不同方言。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence that a machine can read but a poet cannot.
abstract.cn: 想象一句机器读得懂、诗人却读不懂的话。

abstract.en: Picture a grammar book whose examples run when you turn the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一本语法书，翻页时书里的例子就运行起来。

examples.en: A programming language is defined as much by its rules as by its keywords.
examples.cn: 编程语言由规则界定，其重要性不亚于关键字。

examples.en: The team chose a programming language with a strong type system.
examples.cn: 团队选了一门类型系统强的编程语言。

examples.en: Teaching a programming language without projects leaves the syntax abstract.
examples.cn: 教编程语言而不做项目，语法就始终抽象。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑（pro）来（gram）明（ming）＋语言」——把步骤说明白所用的那套语言

root: 希腊 pro-「在前」+ graphein「书写」→ programma → 法语 programme → 英语 program → programming；拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」→ 古法语 langue → 英语 language；两词合为 programming language。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses travel from the general notation to one named language, a family, a formal object of study, and then down and across the scale to low-level, high-level, domain-specific and machine-control notations.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从泛指记号出发，走到某门具名语言、一个语族、一个形式研究对象，再沿尺度下探与横移，落到低级、高级、领域特定与机器控制这几类记号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a board covered with arrows and brackets, with two different dialects circled side by side for comparison.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块写满箭头与括号的白板，两种不同方言被圈在一起作对比。

branches.en: THE NOTATION ITSELF: symbols plus rules for writing what a computer must do.
branches.cn: 记号本身：符号加规则，用来书写计算机该做什么。

branches.en: PARTICULAR AND FAMILY: one named product, and the lineage of products built on one paradigm.
branches.cn: 单个与谱系：一个具名成品，以及建立在同一范式上的一脉成品。

branches.en: FORMAL OBJECT: grammar and meaning written precisely enough to be proved about.
branches.cn: 形式对象：语法与语义被精确到可以作证明的程度。

branches.en: LEVELS: the same phrase covers assembly at one end and named variables at the other.
branches.cn: 层次：同一短语一端涵盖汇编，另一端涵盖具名变量。

branches.en: NARROW USE: from a single problem domain to a single machine that never runs a general system.
branches.cn: 窄用：从单一问题领域到一台从不运行通用系统的机器。

intro.en: The phrase is two complete words joined by English syntax: a Greek-derived noun with -ing, and a Latin-derived noun with its own history.
intro.cn: 这个短语是两个完整单词由英语句法连接：一个希腊来源名词加 -ing，一个拉丁来源名词带着自己的历史。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies lingua for the second half and programma for the first; the English endings -ing and -age do the joining work.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语为后半提供 lingua，为前半提供 programma；英语词尾 -ing 与 -age 承担连接工作。

items.example: The Latin noun covers both the organ and its use.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词同时涵盖器官与其用途。

items.example: English kept the bodily and abstract senses together.
items.exampleCN: 英语把身体义与抽象义留在一起。

items.example: The ending turns langue into a name for a whole system.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 langue 变成整套系统的名称。

items.example: The first half of the phrase descends from it.
items.exampleCN: 短语的前半由它而来。

items.meaning: a plan; a set of instructions
items.example: Programming is built on this base.
items.exampleCN: programming 就建在这个词基上。

items.example: The ending makes the base into the name of a craft.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把词基变成一门手艺的名称。

items.example: The first half of the compound is itself a gerund.
items.exampleCN: 复合词的前半本身就是动名词。

items.meaning: the notation used to write code
items.meaningCN: 写代码所用的记号系统
items.example: The compound separates the notation from the machine and from speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把这套记号与机器、与口语区分开。

items.example: Linguistic study and programming language design borrow from each other.
items.exampleCN: 语言学研究与编程语言设计相互借鉴。

items.example: Markup names the other kind of notation.
items.exampleCN: 标记（markup）指另一类记号。

definition_zh: 算法；解题步骤；计算方法
definition_en: a finite step-by-step procedure for solving a problem or carrying out a computation
core_image: 一张纸上画着一串带箭头的方框，每一步都指向下一步，最后停在一个写有结果的圆里
scene: 纸上画着一串带箭头的方框，每一步都指向下一步，最后停在一个写有结果的圆里。The nurse followed the sorting algorithm step by step until every record was in order.
sceneCN: 这里 algorithm 指为解决某个问题而规定的一串有限步骤（第 1 个义项：解决问题的有限步骤序列）；句意：护士按这套排序算法一步步执行，直到每份记录都归了位。图中可辨识物件：方框、箭头、末端圆框、结果字样。

pos.zh: 算法；解题步骤；计算方法

derivatives.zh: 阿拉伯数字记数法；十进制算法

senses.title: A finite procedure for a problem
senses.definition: a set of steps that always ends and always yields an answer for the allowed inputs
senses.definitionCN: 对允许的输入总能终止并给出答案的一组步骤
senses.example: The manual gives an algorithm for checking every receipt twice.
senses.exampleCN: 手册给出了一套把每张收据核对两遍的算法。
senses.why: the word began as the name of a written calculating method, so its core sense is a method laid out step by step rather than a single trick.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一种写下来的计算方法，核心义因此是按步骤铺开的方法，而不是某个单点窍门。

senses.title: A procedure precise enough for a computer
senses.titleCN: 精确到可交给计算机执行的步骤
senses.definition: a procedure stated so exactly that a machine can carry it out without guessing
senses.definitionCN: 表述得足够精确，机器无需猜测即可执行的步骤
senses.example: The algorithm must say what to do at every branch, not just at the start.
senses.exampleCN: 算法必须说明每个分支该做什么，而不只是开头怎么做。
senses.why: computers removed every human gap in the procedure, so the modern sense stresses total explicitness.
senses.whyCN: 计算机抹掉了步骤中一切由人填补的空隙，现代词义因此强调完全的明确性。

senses.title: The method as an object of study
senses.definition: the abstract object whose running time and memory use can be measured and compared
senses.definitionCN: 可以测量并比较运行时间与内存占用的抽象对象
senses.example: Two algorithm designs can give the same answers at very different costs.
senses.exampleCN: 两种算法设计可以给出相同答案，代价却差得很远。
senses.why: once procedures were written formally, they could be analysed like mathematical objects, and the noun named that object.
senses.whyCN: 步骤一旦被形式化地写出，就能像数学对象一样被分析，名词便指这个对象。

senses.title: A named routine in software
senses.definition: a standard procedure such as sorting or searching, often named after its strategy
senses.definitionCN: 排序、搜索等标准步骤，常按其所用策略命名
senses.example: The sort algorithm merges small lists before joining them.
senses.exampleCN: 这个排序算法先把小列表合并，再把它们接起来。
senses.why: libraries of reusable procedures needed names, and each named procedure was called an algorithm after its method.
senses.whyCN: 可复用的过程库需要名字，每个具名过程依其方法被称为一个算法。

senses.title: A rule set for calculation
senses.definition: a fixed set of rules for performing arithmetic with written numerals
senses.definitionCN: 用写出的数字进行算术运算的固定规则集
senses.example: The medieval algorithm for long division spread with Arabic numerals.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的长除法算法随阿拉伯数字一起传播。
senses.why: the oldest sense is simply the rules of decimal calculation that the word's namesake taught, and this sense survives in the older spelling algorism.
senses.whyCN: 最老的意思就是这个词的同名者所教的十进制计算规则，这一义保存在较早拼写 algorism 里。

senses.title: A decision procedure in logic
senses.definition: a mechanical method that decides, in finitely many steps, whether a statement follows from given rules
senses.definitionCN: 在有限步内判定某陈述是否可由给定规则推出的机械方法
senses.example: No algorithm decides every question in that formal system.
senses.exampleCN: 没有算法能判定该形式系统里的每一个问题。
senses.why: logic borrowed the word for any mechanical decision method, because such a method removes the need for insight at each step.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学借这个词指任何机械判定方法，因为这类方法免去了每一步都要靠洞察。

senses.title: The rule set inside a service
senses.titleCN: 服务内部运行的规则集
senses.definition: the scoring or ranking rules that decide what a platform shows to a user
senses.definitionCN: 决定平台向用户展示什么的评分或排序规则
senses.example: The feed algorithm ranks posts by how long people linger.
senses.exampleCN: 信息流算法按人们停留的时间给帖子排序。
senses.why: platforms turned a formal procedure into a product feature, and users met the word as the invisible rule behind what they see.
senses.whyCN: 平台把形式化步骤变成产品功能，用户于是把这个词理解为眼前内容背后那条看不见的规则。

senses.title: A procedure for routing or scheduling
senses.definition: the rule set a network or system uses to choose paths, times or resources
senses.definitionCN: 网络或系统用来选择路径、时间或资源的规则集
senses.example: The routing algorithm sends each packet along the least crowded link.
senses.exampleCN: 路由算法让每个数据包走最不拥挤的链路。
senses.why: networks must choose among options thousands of times a second, and any such choice rule is naturally called an algorithm.
senses.whyCN: 网络每秒要在众多选项中做出成千上万次选择，这类选择规则自然就叫算法。

senses.title: A recipe for doing something
senses.definition: a fixed, often unthinking way of proceeding in everyday matters
senses.definitionCN: 日常事务中固定、常常无需思考的处理方式
senses.example: There is no algorithm for choosing whom to trust.
senses.exampleCN: 挑选该信任谁，并没有现成的算法。
senses.why: when people say there is no algorithm for something, they mean no reliable step-by-step rule exists, which is the word used in its broadest everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 当人们说某事没有算法时，意思是并不存在可靠的逐步规则，这是这个词最宽泛的日常用法。

intro.en: Algorithm is an eponym: it comes from the Latinised name of the ninth-century mathematician al-Khwarizmi, whose textbook taught decimal calculation. The -th- spelling is a later mistake, not part of the name. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: algorithm 是一个由人名转来的词：出自九世纪数学家花拉子米的拉丁化名字，他的教科书传授十进制计算。词中的 -th- 是后来的误写，并非名字的一部分。年代均为约数。

items.en: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi worked in Baghdad in the ninth century and wrote a treatise on calculation with Indian numerals.
items.cn: 穆罕默德·伊本·穆萨·花拉子米在九世纪的巴格达工作，写有一部讲述用印度数字计算的论著。

items.en: Translators Latinised his name as Algoritmi, which became the label for his calculation method rather than for the man.
items.cn: 译者把他的名字拉丁化为 Algoritmi，这个词后来成了他所教计算法的标签，而不再指这个人。

items.en: Medieval Latin algorismus named the decimal system and the rules for using it, and English algorism came from that form.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 algorismus 指十进制及其使用规则，英语 algorism 即由这一形式而来。

items.en: Writers linked the unfamiliar word to Greek arithmos, number, and altered the spelling to algorithm; the false link is documented and was never corrected.
items.cn: 写作者把这个陌生词与希腊语 arithmos「数」联系起来，把拼写改成 algorithm；这一错误联系有记录，且从未被纠正。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word shifted from written arithmetic rules to any precise procedure that a machine can execute.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个词从书面的算术规则转为指任何机器可以执行的精确步骤。

items.en: Generally accepted: the personal name refers to Khwarazm, a region south of the Aral Sea, which older sources spell in more than one way. The derivation of the word from his name is documented; only the ancient spellings of the place vary.
items.cn: 一般认为是：这个人名指咸海南面的花拉子模地区，古代文献对该地名有不止一种拼写。这个词由他的名字转来有文献依据，可变的只是地名的古代拼写。

note.en: The first group shares the name or the spelling and is easily confused; the second group names neighbouring ideas of method, rule and shortcut.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一人名来源或形近，容易混淆；第二组是与方法、规则、捷径相邻的概念。

entries.definition: The older English word for the decimal system and its calculation rules; algorithm is the later, respelled descendant.
entries.definitionCN: 指十进制及其计算规则的较早英语词；algorithm 是后来改拼的变体。

entries.definition: Relating to algorithms; it describes the method, while algorithm names the method itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「算法的」；它描述方法，而 algorithm 指方法本身。

entries.definition: By means of an algorithm; it modifies how something is done, not what it is.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「按算法地」；它修饰做事方式，不指事物本身。

entries.definition: A mathematical exponent word built from Greek logos and arithmos; the shared ending is coincidence of spelling, not shared origin.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊语 logos 与 arithmos 构成的数学指数词；相同词尾只是拼写巧合，并非同源。

entries.definition: Any agreed way of doing something; an algorithm is a procedure precise enough to be executed mechanically.
entries.definitionCN: 任何约定俗成的做法；algorithm 是精确到可机械执行的 procedure。

entries.definition: A way of working, often with judgment left to the user; an algorithm removes that judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 工作方式，常给使用者留出判断空间；algorithm 则取消这种判断。

entries.definition: A shortcut that usually works but has no guarantee; an algorithm promises a result for every allowed input.
entries.definitionCN: 通常有效但无保证的捷径；algorithm 则承诺对每个允许输入都给出结果。

entries.definition: The concrete code a machine runs; an algorithm is the method that the code implements, and one algorithm can be coded many ways.
entries.definitionCN: 机器运行的具体代码；algorithm 是代码所实现的方法，同一种算法可以有多种写法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real personal name, the real older spelling and the real computing phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的人名来源、真实的较早拼写与真实的计算机搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is a person: al-Khwarizmi taught the rules of calculation, and his Latinised name became the name of the rules.
normal.cn: 这个词来自一个人：花拉子米教计算规则，他的拉丁化名字就成了规则的名字。

normal.en: The older spelling algorism still means decimal calculation; algorithm is the respelled branch.
normal.cn: 较早拼写 algorism 仍指十进制计算；algorithm 是改拼后的分支。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the computing sense: sorting algorithm, search algorithm, encryption algorithm.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出计算机义：排序算法、搜索算法、加密算法。

normal.en: The -th- came from a mistaken link to Greek arithmos, number, and it stuck.
normal.cn: 词中的 -th- 来自与希腊语 arithmos「数」的错误联系，而且一直沿用下来。

normal.en: A logarithm looks like an algorithm but belongs to a different Greek family.
normal.cn: logarithm 看起来像 algorithm，却属于另一个希腊词族。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor of doors, each opening only after the one before has closed.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊，每扇门都要前一扇关上后才打开。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe that refuses to end until the pot is exactly full.
abstract.cn: 想象一份菜谱，锅没正好装满就绝不肯结束。

abstract.en: Picture a sorting hat that never asks for a second opinion.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶分院帽，从不征询第二个意见。

examples.en: The same algorithm can be written in five languages and still do the same work.
examples.cn: 同一个算法可以用五种语言写出，做的事仍然一样。

examples.en: A good algorithm says what to do when the input is empty.
examples.cn: 好的算法会说明输入为空时该怎么办。

examples.en: The team measured the algorithm's cost before adding more data.
examples.cn: 团队在增加数据之前先测了这套算法的开销。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱（al）哥（go）算（rith）法（m）」——爱算的哥们，一步步算到底

root: 九世纪数学家 al-Khwārizmī 之名 → 拉丁化 Algoritmi → 中世纪拉丁 algorismus → 英语 algorism；拼写受希腊语 arithmos「数」误类推而改为 algorithm。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one idea: a written method of calculation becomes any finite procedure, then a precise machine procedure, a formal object, a named routine, a decision rule, a product rule, a network rule and finally a recipe for life.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一个念头展开：一种写下来的计算方法，变成任何有限步骤，再变成精确的机器步骤、形式对象、具名例程、判定规则、产品规则、网络规则，最后变成生活里的套路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain of boxes joined by arrows, each step pointing to the next and ending in a single result.
core.cn: 核心意象：方框由箭头串起，每一步指向下一步，最后收在一个结果上。

branches.en: THE OLDEST LAYER: written rules for decimal arithmetic, preserved in the spelling algorism.
branches.cn: 最老的一层：书面的十进制运算规则，保存在拼写 algorism 里。

branches.en: PROCEDURE: steps that always end, and steps explicit enough for a machine to follow without guessing.
branches.cn: 步骤：总会终止的步骤，以及明确到机器无需猜测就能执行的步骤。

branches.en: OBJECT AND ROUTINE: the same procedure studied as a mathematical object and shipped as a named library routine.
branches.cn: 对象与例程：同一套步骤既作为数学对象被研究，又作为具名库例程被交付。

branches.en: DECIDING AND ROUTING: logic and networks both use mechanical rules to choose among possibilities.
branches.cn: 判定与路由：逻辑学与网络都用机械规则在多种可能中作选择。

branches.en: EVERYDAY RULE: a platform's ranking rule and a personal recipe are both the word at its broadest.
branches.cn: 日常规则：平台的排序规则与个人的做事套路，都是这个词最宽泛的用法。

intro.en: Algorithm is not built from Latin or Greek roots but from a Latinised Arabic personal name; later spellings and endings were added by English and by a mistaken Greek link.
intro.cn: algorithm 并非由拉丁或希腊词根构成，而是来自拉丁化的阿拉伯人名；后来的拼写与词尾是英语加上去的，另有一处希腊语误联。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin algorismus is the bridge form; the Greek arithmos that reshaped the spelling is a false association, not a real element.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 algorismus 是中间的桥接形式；改写拼写的希腊语 arithmos 是错误联想，并非真实构件。

items.example: The article is frozen into the Latinised name.
items.exampleCN: 这个冠词被冻进了拉丁化的人名里。

items.example: The nisba identifies the scholar by his region.
items.exampleCN: 这个名字后缀用地名标识这位学者。

items.structure: Latinised form of the Arabic name
items.meaningCN: 这位学者名字的拉丁写法
items.example: Translators used the name for the method.
items.exampleCN: 译者用这个名字来指那套方法。

items.meaning: the decimal system and its rules
items.example: The Latin noun became English algorism.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词成了英语 algorism。

items.example: The Greek word pulled the spelling toward -th- by mistake.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词把拼写误拉向 -th-。

items.example: Algorism is the older doublet of algorithm.
items.exampleCN: algorism 是 algorithm 的较早同源异形词。

items.example: The respelling attached the word to number.
items.exampleCN: 这次改拼把词与「数」挂上了钩。

items.example: Algorithmic describes anything driven by such a procedure.
items.exampleCN: algorithmic 描述由这类步骤驱动的事物。

items.example: Algorithmically means by running the procedure.
items.exampleCN: algorithmically 意为「按算法执行」。

items.example: Algorithmics names the theory of procedures.
items.exampleCN: algorithmics 指关于步骤的理论。

definition_zh: 算法的；由算法驱动的；按固定步骤运作的
definition_en: relating to, produced by, or organized according to an algorithm
core_image: 一排排数据流沿看不见的轨道被分拣进不同的槽口
scene: 一排排数据流沿看不见的轨道被分拣进不同的槽口，槽口上方没有一只手在操作。The ranking of search results is now largely algorithmic rather than editorial.
sceneCN: 这里 algorithmic 指由算法而非人工编辑决定的（第 3 个义项：由算法产生的）；句意：搜索结果的排序如今主要由算法决定，而不是由编辑决定。图中可辨识物件：数据流、轨道、槽口、分流闸。

pos.zh: 算法的；由算法产生的；按固定步骤的

senses.title: Relating to an algorithm
senses.definition: concerning the method or the steps of a procedure rather than its raw result
senses.definitionCN: 关于方法或步骤本身，而不是其直接结果
senses.example: The paper explains the algorithmic side of the system, not its hardware.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文解释系统的算法层面，而非硬件。
senses.why: the adjective simply tags whatever belongs to an algorithm, so its plainest job is to mark that domain.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词就是给属于算法的事物贴标签，最基本的作用是标出那个领域。

senses.title: Expressed as formal steps
senses.definition: written as a precise sequence that can be checked step by step
senses.definitionCN: 写成可逐步核对的精确序列
senses.example: The solution is algorithmic: it lists the moves instead of arguing for them.
senses.exampleCN: 这个解法是算法式的：它列出步骤，而不是为步骤辩护。
senses.why: to call something algorithmic is to say it can be laid out as checkable steps, not left as intuition.
senses.whyCN: 说某事物是算法式的，等于说它能被铺成可核对的步骤，而非停留在直觉。

senses.title: Produced by a running algorithm
senses.titleCN: 由运行中的算法产生的
senses.definition: generated or selected by a computer procedure rather than by a person
senses.definitionCN: 由计算机程序生成或挑选，而非由人产生
senses.example: Your feed is algorithmic, assembled from your own clicks.
senses.exampleCN: 你看到的信息流是算法生成的，由你自己的点击拼装而成。
senses.why: when the procedure runs on data, its output is naturally described with the adjective, which is how the word entered daily speech.
senses.whyCN: 当步骤在数据上运行，其产物自然用这个形容词来描述，这个词就这样进入日常语言。

senses.title: Governed by rules, not judgment
senses.definition: decided by fixed rules so that individual discretion plays little part
senses.definitionCN: 由固定规则决定，个人裁量几乎不起作用
senses.example: The allocation is algorithmic and cannot be adjusted case by case.
senses.exampleCN: 分配是按算法走的，不能逐例调整。
senses.why: the adjective also criticises systems that hide judgment inside rules, even when no computer is involved.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也用来批评把判断藏进规则的系统，哪怕根本不涉及计算机。

senses.title: Measured by cost and complexity
senses.titleCN: 按开销与复杂度衡量的
senses.definition: describing the time or memory a procedure needs as its input grows
senses.definitionCN: 描述输入增大时步骤所需时间或内存的变化
senses.example: The algorithmic cost grew faster than the data did.
senses.exampleCN: 算法的开销增长得比数据还快。
senses.why: the study of procedures measures them, and the adjective names that measured property.
senses.whyCN: 对步骤的研究要对它作度量，形容词就指这种被度量的性质。

senses.title: Mechanical and repeatable
senses.definition: carried out the same way every time, with no room for variation
senses.definitionCN: 每次都按同样方式执行，没有变动余地
senses.example: The checking is algorithmic, so two reviewers get identical results.
senses.exampleCN: 核对是按算法做的，所以两位复核者得到相同结果。
senses.why: the defining virtue of a procedure is that it repeats exactly, and the adjective praises or warns about that sameness.
senses.whyCN: 步骤的根本优点是能精确重复，形容词对这种一致性或褒或贬。

senses.title: Generating art from rules
senses.definition: describing art or music whose form is generated by a set of rules
senses.definitionCN: 指形式由一组规则生成的艺术或音乐
senses.example: The gallery showed algorithmic drawings that no hand had drawn.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊展出了并非由手绘出的算法绘画。
senses.why: artists who hand a rule set to a machine produce works whose authorship sits in the rules, hence the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 把规则集交给机器的艺术家，其作者性落在规则上，于是有了这个形容词。

senses.title: Concerning fairness of automated decisions
senses.titleCN: 关于自动决策的公平性
senses.definition: used of the bias, transparency or accountability of automated decisions
senses.definitionCN: 用于指自动决策的偏见、透明度或问责
senses.example: The report examined algorithmic harms in hiring tools.
senses.exampleCN: 报告考察了招聘工具中的算法危害。
senses.why: as automated decisions spread, the adjective became a label for the political question of who answers for them.
senses.whyCN: 随着自动决策扩散，这个形容词成了「谁来负责」这一政治问题的标签。

intro.en: Algorithmic is algorithm plus the adjective ending -ic, which English took from Greek through Latin. The base word itself is an eponym from the mathematician al-Khwarizmi. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: algorithmic 是 algorithm 加形容词词尾 -ic，后者经拉丁语来自希腊语。词基本身是由数学家花拉子米之名转来的词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Algorithm descends from the Latinised name Algoritmi, given to the calculation method taught by al-Khwarizmi in the ninth century.
items.cn: algorithm 出自拉丁化人名 Algoritmi，本是九世纪花拉子米所教计算法的名称。

items.en: The base was later respelled after Greek arithmos, number, by a false association that became permanent.
items.cn: 词基后来因与希腊语 arithmos「数」的错误联系而改拼，这一改动沿用至今。

items.en: The ending -ic goes back to Greek -ikos, meaning relating to, which Latin passed on as -icus and French and English shortened to -ic.
items.cn: 词尾 -ic 可追到希腊语 -ikos「与……有关的」，拉丁语作 -icus 传下，法语与英语缩为 -ic。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in the nineteenth century, when the noun still meant calculation rules; it described anything done by such rules.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十九世纪已有记录，当时名词仍指计算规则，形容词描述按这类规则进行的事物。

items.en: With computers the adjective moved to procedures, complexity, trading and ranking, and later to the social questions raised by automated decisions.
items.cn: 有了计算机之后，这个形容词转向步骤、复杂度、交易与排序，后来又转向自动决策引发的社会问题。

items.en: The base from Algoritmi and the ending from Greek -ikos through Latin -icus are both documented. The earliest use of the English adjective is dated only approximately, and any older Indo-European source for -ikos is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：词基出自 Algoritmi，词尾经拉丁语 -icus 出自希腊语 -ikos，两段都有文献依据；英语形容词最早使用的年代只有约数，-ikos 更早的印欧语来源属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is the same base in other shapes; the second group names neighbouring descriptions of rule-bound and automated behaviour.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词基的其他形式；第二组是与「受规则约束」「自动化」相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The procedure itself; the adjective describes what belongs to or comes from it.
entries.definitionCN: 指步骤本身；形容词描述属于它或由它而来的事物。

entries.definition: By running a procedure; it answers how, while the adjective answers what kind.
entries.definitionCN: 意为按算法执行；副词回答「怎样」，形容词回答「哪一类」。

entries.definition: The study of procedures and their costs; it is a discipline, not a description.
entries.definitionCN: 研究步骤及其开销的学科；它是学科名，不是描述词。

entries.definition: The older word for decimal calculation; it shares the origin but not the computing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指十进制计算的较早词；同源，但没有计算机义。

entries.definition: Working by itself once set going; it stresses independence from a hand, while algorithmic stresses the rule being followed.
entries.definitionCN: 设定后自行运作；强调无需人手，而 algorithmic 强调所遵循的规则。

entries.definition: Involving calculation by computer; it names the machinery of doing, algorithmic names the method's form.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过计算机计算；它指做的机器手段，algorithmic 指方法的形式。

entries.definition: Built on stated rules, whether or not a machine runs them; algorithmic usually implies execution by a procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 建立在明示规则上，不论是否由机器执行；algorithmic 通常暗示由程序执行。

entries.definition: Done in a fixed, unthinking way; close to one sense of algorithmic, but it carries a stronger tone of dullness.
entries.definitionCN: 以固定、不加思考的方式做；接近 algorithmic 的一义，但更带呆板色彩。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real base noun, the real ending and the real phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的基础名词、真实的词尾与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Algorithm plus -ic: the ending means relating to, so algorithmic means belonging to an algorithm.
normal.cn: algorithm 加 -ic：词尾意为「与……有关」，所以 algorithmic 就是属于算法的。

normal.en: The family runs algorithm, algorithmic, algorithmically and algorithmics.
normal.cn: 同族词有 algorithm、algorithmic、algorithmically 与 algorithmics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the modern uses: algorithmic trading, algorithmic bias, algorithmic recommendation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出现代用法：算法交易、算法偏见、算法推荐。

normal.en: The base is a person's name, so the adjective literally means in the manner of al-Khwarizmi's rules.
normal.cn: 词基是人名，因此这个形容词字面上就是「按花拉子米的规则来」。

normal.en: Greek -ikos became Latin -icus and English -ic, so the ending simply means relating to.
normal.cn: 希腊语 -ikos 变成拉丁语 -icus 与英语 -ic，词尾意思就是「与……有关」。

abstract.en: Picture a river that chooses its own channels without a digger.
abstract.cn: 想象一条没有挖掘者却自己选道的河。

abstract.en: Picture a judge who never explains, only applies.
abstract.cn: 想象一位从不解释、只作适用的法官。

abstract.en: Picture a painting that keeps painting itself after the artist leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅在画家离开后仍继续画自己的画。

examples.en: Algorithmic sorting decides the order before any editor sees the list.
examples.cn: 算法排序在编辑看到清单之前就决定了顺序。

examples.en: The company publishes an algorithmic audit every year.
examples.cn: 公司每年公布一份算法审计报告。

examples.en: Her algorithmic music is generated from a few simple rules.
examples.cn: 她的算法音乐由几条简单规则生成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱（al）哥（go）算（rith）米（mic）」——爱算的哥们按米粒般的步骤办事，就是算法式的

root: al-Khwārizmī 之名 → 拉丁 Algoritmi → algorismus → algorism/algorithm；再加希腊—拉丁形容词词尾 -ic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from plain attribution to formal steps, generated output, rule-bound decisions, measured cost, mechanical repetition, generative art and finally the fairness of automated choices.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单纯的归属关系，走到形式步骤、生成产物、受规则支配的决策、被度量的开销、机械重复、生成艺术，最后走到自动选择的公平问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: streams of data sliding along invisible rails into slots, with no hand anywhere in the picture.
core.cn: 核心意象：数据流沿看不见的轨道滑进槽口，画面里没有任何一只手。

branches.en: ATTRIBUTION AND FORM: belonging to a procedure, and laid out as checkable steps.
branches.cn: 归属与形式：属于某种步骤，并被铺成可核对的步骤。

branches.en: OUTPUT AND SAMENESS: what the procedure produces, and the exact repetition that makes it trustworthy or cold.
branches.cn: 产物与一致：步骤产出的东西，以及使它可信或冷冰冰的精确重复。

branches.en: RULE OVER JUDGMENT: discretion disappears into fixed rules, even without a machine.
branches.cn: 规则压过判断：裁量消失于固定规则，哪怕没有机器。

branches.en: COST: procedures are compared by the time and memory they need as input grows.
branches.cn: 开销：步骤按输入增大时所需的时间与内存被比较。

branches.en: CULTURE AND POLITICS: rules generate art, and automated choices raise the question of who answers for them.
branches.cn: 文化与政治：规则生成艺术，自动选择则提出谁来负责的问题。

intro.en: The word is a name-derived base plus a Greek adjective ending that reached English through Latin and French.
intro.cn: 这个词是人名来源的词基加一个希腊形容词词尾，后者经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin algorismus supplies the base; Latin -icus supplies the shape of the ending, which English shortened.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 algorismus 提供词基；拉丁语 -icus 提供词尾的外形，英语再把它缩短。

items.example: The Latin noun is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是整个词族的词基。

items.example: The Greek word caused the -th- respelling by mistake.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词误改了拼写，加进 -th-。

items.example: The noun supplies the meaning the adjective carries.
items.exampleCN: 名词提供形容词所承载的意义。

items.example: The ending turns a thing into a description.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把事物变成描述词。

items.example: Algorithmically means by running the procedure.
items.exampleCN: algorithmically 意为按算法运行。

items.example: Algorithmics studies procedures and their costs.
items.exampleCN: algorithmics 研究步骤及其开销。

items.example: Algorism names the old calculation practice.
items.exampleCN: algorism 指旧的计算做法。

items.meaning: relating to or produced by a procedure
items.meaningCN: 与算法有关的或由算法产生的
items.example: The word now covers trading, art and bias.
items.exampleCN: 这个词如今涵盖交易、艺术与偏见。

items.example: The list is ordered algorithmically.
items.exampleCN: 清单按算法排序。

definition_zh: 数据库；资料库；数据库系统
definition_en: an organized collection of data, or the system that stores and lets users query it
core_image: 一排排抽屉整齐编号，每格卡片上写着同一类信息，拉手一抽就能取到
scene: 档案室里一排排抽屉整齐编号，每格卡片上写着同一类信息，管理员按编号就能抽出想要的记录。The hospital keeps every patient record in a single database.
sceneCN: 这里 database 指按统一方式组织、可供检索的数据集合（第 1 个义项：有组织的数据集合）；句意：这家医院把所有病人的记录保存在一个数据库里。图中可辨识物件：编号抽屉、卡片、档案架、借阅记录。

senses.title: An organized collection of data
senses.definition: data arranged so that items can be stored, found and updated reliably
senses.definitionCN: 经过安排、使条目能被可靠存入、查找与更新的数据
senses.example: The lab built a database of every sample it had tested.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室为它测过的每个样本建立了一个数据库。
senses.why: data plus base: the word calls the collection a foundation on which records rest, so its core is organized storage rather than a single file.
senses.whyCN: data 加 base：这个词把数据集合称为记录赖以承载的基础，核心义是有组织的存储，而不是单个文件。

senses.title: The software that manages it
senses.definition: a program or system that stores records and answers queries about them
senses.definitionCN: 存储记录并回答查询的程序或系统
senses.example: The database answers a query without reading every record.
senses.exampleCN: 数据库无需读取每条记录就能回答一次查询。
senses.why: users often name the whole system by the collection it holds, so the software and the store share one word.
senses.whyCN: 使用者常用所存内容来称整个系统，于是软件与存储共用一个词。

senses.title: One particular instance
senses.definition: a single named store belonging to one organisation or application
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个组织或应用的具名存储
senses.example: The customer database was copied before the upgrade.
senses.exampleCN: 升级之前先复制了客户数据库。
senses.why: every installation is countable and named, so database also means this one store, not the idea of stores in general.
senses.whyCN: 每套安装都可数且具名，因此 database 也指这一个库，而不是泛指的存储概念。

senses.title: A body of facts on a subject
senses.definition: a large organized body of information consulted for reference
senses.definitionCN: 为查阅而整理的大规模信息总体
senses.example: The dictionary is backed by a database of two million examples.
senses.exampleCN: 这部词典背后有一个两百万例句的数据库。
senses.why: the computing word spread to any reference collection organized for lookup, even one read by people.
senses.whyCN: 计算机词扩散到任何为查阅而整理的信息集合，哪怕是供人阅读的。

senses.title: Structured tables with a schema
senses.definition: data held in tables with declared fields and relationships between them
senses.definitionCN: 存放在表中、字段已声明并带相互关系的数据
senses.example: The database stores orders and customers in linked tables.
senses.exampleCN: 这个数据库把订单与客户存在相互关联的表中。
senses.why: relational design gave the word a precise technical sense: structure declared in advance, not just data piled together.
senses.whyCN: 关系型设计赋予这个词精确的技术含义：结构事先声明，而不是数据堆在一起。

senses.title: A research repository
senses.definition: a curated collection shared by a research community for reuse
senses.definitionCN: 由研究群体维护、供重复使用的精选集合
senses.example: The genomic database collects sequences from a hundred laboratories.
senses.exampleCN: 这个基因组数据库收集了上百个实验室的序列。
senses.why: science needed shared reference collections, and borrowed the computing word for them.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要共享的参考集合，于是借用了这个计算机词。

senses.title: The store behind an application
senses.definition: the persistent store an application reads from and writes to
senses.definitionCN: 应用读取与写入的持久存储
senses.example: Every saved draft goes into the database before the page closes.
senses.exampleCN: 每份保存的草稿都在页面关闭前进入数据库。
senses.why: in software, the database is the place where state survives between sessions, which is why it is named separately from the program.
senses.whyCN: 在软件里，数据库是状态在两次会话之间存活的地方，因此它与程序分开命名。

senses.title: A mental or informal store
senses.titleCN: 口中的「脑子里的资料库」
senses.definition: used loosely for any large personal or shared stock of remembered facts
senses.definitionCN: 宽泛指个人或群体记住的大量事实
senses.example: She has a database of every colleague's birthday in her head.
senses.exampleCN: 她脑子里存着每位同事生日的资料库。
senses.why: the word became a metaphor for organized memory, which is how technical vocabulary usually enters ordinary speech.
senses.whyCN: 这个词成了有组织记忆的比喻，技术词汇通常就是这样进入日常语言的。

intro.en: Database is a twentieth-century English compound of data, the plural of Latin datum, and base, from Greek basis. It was coined in the early 1960s for computer-held records. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: database 是二十世纪的英语复合词，由拉丁语 datum 的复数 data 与出自希腊语 basis 的 base 组成。它在 1960 年代初被造出来，指计算机保存的记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Datum is the neuter past participle of dare, to give: literally something given, hence a fact granted to an argument.
items.cn: datum 是 dare「给予」的中性过去分词：字面即「被给予的东西」，引申为提供给论证的事实。

items.en: English borrowed data as the plural of datum, then treated it as a mass noun; both uses remain, and style guides differ.
items.cn: 英语借入 data 作为 datum 的复数，随后又把它当不可数名词用；两种用法都还在，各文体指南的处理并不一致。

items.en: Greek basis meant a step or a pedestal, from bainein, to go; Latin basis kept the image of a footing, and English base is its shortened form.
items.cn: 希腊语 basis 指步伐或底座，出自 bainein「行走」；拉丁语 basis 保留了「立足处」的意象，英语 base 是它的缩短形式。

items.en: Database was coined in the early 1960s as one word for a structured body of machine-readable records, replacing longer phrases then in use.
items.cn: database 在 1960 年代初被造为一个单词，指机器可读的结构化记录总体，取代了当时在用的更长说法。

items.en: As database management systems spread, database came to name the software as well as the stored collection.
items.cn: 随着数据库管理系统普及，database 既指存储的数据集合，也指管理它的软件。

items.en: The first half from Latin datum and the second from Greek basis are both documented, and the compound is a coinage of the early 1960s. The decade of the coinage is approximate, and any older Indo-European source for bainein is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：前半出自拉丁语 datum，后半出自希腊语 basis，两段都有文献依据，复合词是 1960 年代初的新造词；造词年代只有约数，bainein 更早的印欧语来源属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is the data family in other shapes; the second group names neighbouring ways of storing and consulting information.
note.cn: 第一组是数据词族的其他形式；第二组是与存储、查阅信息相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The facts themselves; a database is the organized place where those facts are kept and queried.
entries.definitionCN: 指事实本身；database 是保存并查询这些事实的有组织场所。

entries.definition: A specific collection prepared for analysis or training; it may live inside a database but is usually a fixed extract.
entries.definitionCN: 为分析或训练准备好的特定集合；它可能存放在数据库里，但通常是一份固定摘录。

entries.definition: A large store of data, often used for reference collections; the older word overlaps with database but is less tied to software.
entries.definitionCN: 大型数据存储，常用于参考集合；这个较早的词与 database 有重叠，但与软件的绑定较弱。

entries.definition: A foundation or lower part; alone it says nothing about data, which is why the compound needed both halves.
entries.definitionCN: 指基础或底部；单独使用时与数据无关，所以复合词需要两半合起来。

entries.definition: A place where things are stored and can be retrieved; broader than database and not necessarily electronic.
entries.definitionCN: 存放并可取回物品的场所；比 database 宽，不一定是电子的。

entries.definition: A store of records kept for their long-term value; an archive preserves, a database serves current queries.
entries.definitionCN: 因其长期价值而保存记录的存储；档案重在保存，数据库重在当前查询。
