entries.definition: In computing, a large store built by combining many sources for analysis; it is usually fed from databases.
entries.definitionCN: 计算机中指汇总多个来源、供分析使用的大型存储；它的数据通常来自各个数据库。

entries.definition: An official list kept for a purpose, such as births or licences; narrower and usually authoritative.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定目的保存的官方名录，如出生或执照登记；更窄，且通常具权威性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces and the real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Data plus base: the data are the contents and the base is the footing they rest on.
normal.cn: data 加 base：数据是内容，base 是它们立足的底座。

normal.en: Datum is Latin for something given, so data are the given facts.
normal.cn: datum 在拉丁语里是「被给予的东西」，所以 data 就是被给出的事实。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technology: relational database, database management system, database design.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术面：关系型数据库、数据库管理系统、数据库设计。

normal.en: The family runs data, datum, database, databank and dataset.
normal.cn: 同族词有 data、datum、database、databank 与 dataset。

normal.en: A database is countable: one hospital can keep several databases.
normal.cn: database 可数：一家医院可以有好几个数据库。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of numbered drawers where every card knows its neighbours.
abstract.cn: 想象一面编号抽屉墙，每张卡片都认得自己的邻居。

abstract.en: Picture a library whose shelves rearrange themselves as you walk.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，你边走书架边自己重排。

abstract.en: Picture a memory kept in drawers rather than in a head.
abstract.cn: 想象一份记忆不放在脑袋里，而放在抽屉里。

examples.en: The team moved the old records into a single database.
examples.cn: 团队把旧记录迁入了一个数据库。

examples.en: A database can refuse a malformed record before it is saved.
examples.cn: 数据库可以在保存前拒绝格式错误的记录。

examples.en: The public database lets anyone search the measurements.
examples.cn: 这个公开数据库让任何人都能检索这些测量数据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「得（da）他（ta）贝（base）」——得到他的底账，就是数据库

root: 拉丁 dare「给予」→ datum「被给予的东西」→ 复数 data「数据」；希腊 bainein「行走」→ basis「底座」→ 拉丁 basis → 英语 base；data 与 base 合为 database。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the organized collection to the software, a named instance, a subject reference, structured tables, a research repository, the store behind an app, and finally a metaphor for memory.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从有组织的集合出发，走到管理软件、具名实例、主题资料、结构化表、科研资料库、应用背后的存储，最后走到记忆的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rows of numbered drawers holding cards of one kind, each retrievable by its number.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排排编号抽屉装着同一类卡片，按编号就能取出。

branches.en: STORE AND SYSTEM: the collection of data and the software that keeps it queryable.
branches.cn: 集合与系统：数据集合，以及使它可被查询的软件。

branches.en: COUNTABLE INSTANCE: each installation is one named database with its own copy.
branches.cn: 可数实例：每套安装都是一个具名数据库，有自己的副本。

branches.en: REFERENCE: subject collections and shared research repositories are consulted rather than written to.
branches.cn: 查阅：主题资料与共享科研库主要供查阅，而非写入。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: declared fields and links turn a pile of records into a relational database.
branches.cn: 结构：声明字段与关联，把一堆记录变成关系型数据库。

branches.en: PERSISTENCE AND METAPHOR: it outlives the session, and is borrowed to describe organized memory.
branches.cn: 持久与比喻：它比会话活得久，又被借去描述有组织的记忆。

intro.en: Database is two old borrowings joined: data from Latin dare, and base from Greek basis through Latin. The compound itself is modern English.
intro.cn: database 是两个古老借词的结合：data 出自拉丁语 dare，base 出自希腊语 basis 经拉丁语；复合本身是现代英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies datum, data and basis; the shortening of basis to base happened in Old French and English, not in Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供 datum、data 与 basis；basis 缩为 base 发生在古法语与英语里，而不是拉丁语里。

items.example: The verb supplies the idea that data are given.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「数据是被给出的」这一观念。

items.example: One fact is one datum.
items.exampleCN: 一个事实就是一个数据点。

items.example: English treats data as plural or as a mass noun.
items.exampleCN: 英语把 data 当复数或不可数名词。

items.example: The noun names what something stands on.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指某物所立足之处。

items.structure: basis through Latin and Old French
items.example: The shortened form is the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 缩短形式是复合词的后半。

items.structure: data plus base, coined in the 1960s
items.example: The compound replaced longer phrases for machine files.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词取代了描述机器文件的更长说法。

items.example: Dataset applies the same pattern to one prepared collection.
items.exampleCN: dataset 用同一模式指一份准备好的集合。

items.example: Databank and dataset both begin with this combining form.
items.exampleCN: databank 与 dataset 都以这一组合形式开头。

items.meaning: a place where things are kept
items.example: Databank borrows the image of a stored reserve.
items.exampleCN: databank 借用了储备库的意象。

definition_en: a collection of related data treated as a single unit for analysis, training or publication
core_image: 一张长桌上摊开一叠整齐的表格，每行一条记录，每列一个字段
scene: 长桌上摊开一叠整齐的表格，每行一条记录，每列一个字段，页脚印着这份材料的名称与版本。The researchers released the dataset along with the code that cleaned it.
sceneCN: 这里 dataset 指作为一个整体处理的一批相关数据（第 1 个义项：被当作整体处理的相关数据集合）；句意：研究者连同清洗它的代码一起发布了这份数据集。图中可辨识物件：表格、行、列、页脚标注。

senses.title: A collection treated as one unit
senses.titleCN: 作为一个整体处理的数据集合
senses.definition: related records grouped together so that they can be handled, moved or described as one thing
senses.definitionCN: 把相关记录归在一起，以便作为一件东西处理、搬运或描述
senses.example: The dataset holds ten years of rainfall for one valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这份数据集收录了某个山谷十年的降雨记录。
senses.why: data plus set: a set is a group counted as one, so the compound's core sense is data handled as a single unit.
senses.whyCN: data 加 set：集合是被当作一个来数的组，因此核心义是被当成一个单位处理的数据。

senses.title: The unit fed to a model
senses.definition: the body of examples used to train or evaluate a machine-learning model
senses.definitionCN: 用于训练或评估机器学习模型的样本总体
senses.example: The model saw only a small dataset before it was tested.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型在测试前只见过一份小数据集。
senses.why: machine learning needs a fixed body of examples per run, and that body is naturally named with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 机器学习每次运行需要一份固定的样本总体，这份总体自然沿用同一个词。

senses.title: A benchmark for comparison
senses.definition: a standard collection on which competing methods are scored so that results can be compared
senses.definitionCN: 让不同方法在同一批数据上打分、从而可比结果的标准化集合
senses.example: Every team reported accuracy on the same benchmark dataset.
senses.exampleCN: 每个团队都在同一个基准数据集上报告准确率。
senses.why: fair comparison requires a shared collection, and that shared collection becomes a named dataset.
senses.whyCN: 公平比较需要共享的集合，这份共享集合就成了具名的数据集。

senses.title: Observations from a study
senses.definition: the records collected in a survey, experiment or field study
senses.definitionCN: 在调查、实验或实地研究中收集的记录
senses.example: The survey dataset covers four thousand households.
senses.exampleCN: 这份调查数据集覆盖四千个家庭。
senses.why: statistics has long spoken of a data set as the observations gathered for one analysis, independent of computers.
senses.whyCN: 统计学早就把为一次分析收集的观测称为数据集，这与计算机无关。

senses.title: A published, reusable collection
senses.titleCN: 公开发布可复用的集合
senses.definition: a collection released with documentation so that others can reuse it
senses.definitionCN: 连同说明文档一起发布、供他人复用的集合
senses.example: The open dataset has a licence and a version number.
senses.exampleCN: 这份开放数据集有许可证和版本号。
senses.why: shared research made the collection itself a citable object, so the word now names a published artifact.
senses.whyCN: 共享研究使集合本身成为可引用的成果，因此这个词也指公开发布的产物。

senses.title: One split of a larger collection
senses.definition: one of the parts into which data are divided, such as a training or test portion
senses.definitionCN: 数据被分成的某一份，如训练部分或测试部分
senses.example: The validation dataset was kept apart until the final week.
senses.exampleCN: 验证数据集一直单独留到最后一周。
senses.why: when one collection is split, each part is still called a dataset, with an adjective naming its role.
senses.whyCN: 一份集合被切开后，每一份仍叫 dataset，只加形容词标明它的角色。

senses.title: A structured file with schema
senses.definition: a file whose rows and fields are declared and described by accompanying metadata
senses.definitionCN: 行与字段已声明、并有随附元数据说明的文件
senses.example: The dataset ships with a schema for every column.
senses.exampleCN: 这份数据集为每一列附带了结构说明。
senses.why: a collection becomes usable only when its structure is stated, so the file plus its description is treated as the dataset.
senses.whyCN: 集合只有说清结构才可用，因此文件连同说明一起被当作数据集。

senses.title: A citable item in a repository
senses.definition: a named, identified collection that can be cited by a persistent identifier
senses.definitionCN: 带有持久标识、可被引用的具名集合
senses.example: The paper cites a dataset archived outside the journal.
senses.exampleCN: 论文引用了一份存档在期刊之外的数据集。
senses.why: repositories gave collections identities, and an identified collection is spoken of as a dataset rather than as data in general.
senses.whyCN: 数据仓库给集合以身份，而有了身份的集合就被称为某份数据集，而不是泛泛的数据。

intro.en: Dataset is a modern English compound of data, from Latin datum, and set, a native English noun. The two-word spelling data set is older than the joined form. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: dataset 是现代英语复合词，由出自拉丁语 datum 的 data 与英语本族名词 set 组成。分开写的 data set 比连写形式更早。年代均为约数。

items.en: Datum, something given, is the neuter past participle of dare, to give; its plural data reached English as a mass of facts.
items.cn: datum「被给予的东西」是 dare「给予」的中性过去分词；其复数 data 以大量事实之意进入英语。

items.en: Set is native English, from Old English settan, to place or put; as a noun it means a group of things belonging together.
items.cn: set 是英语本族词，出自上古英语 settan「放置」；作名词时指归在一起的一组事物。

items.en: Statisticians spoke of a data set long before computing, meaning the observations gathered for one analysis.
items.cn: 统计学家早在计算机之前就说 data set，指为一次分析收集的观测。

items.en: The joined form dataset spread with machine-readable files in the late twentieth century, when the collection became a portable object.
items.cn: 连写形式 dataset 随机器可读文件在二十世纪后期扩散，此时集合成了可搬运的对象。

items.en: Training and test datasets gave the word a fixed role in modelling, and benchmark datasets made it citable.
items.cn: 训练与测试数据集让这个词在建模中获得固定角色，基准数据集又使它成为可引用的对象。

items.en: The first half from Latin datum and the second from Old English settan are both documented. The date at which the joined spelling became common is approximate, and any older Indo-European source for dare or settan is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：前半出自拉丁语 datum，后半出自上古英语 settan，两段都有文献依据；连写形式普及的年代只有约数，dare 与 settan 更早的印欧语来源属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is the same data family plus near-spellings; the second group names neighbouring collections used in analysis.
note.cn: 第一组是数据词族及形近词；第二组是分析中使用的相邻集合概念。

entries.definition: The same thing written as two words; the spaced form is older and still used in statistics writing.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个东西的分写形式；分写更早，统计写作中仍在使用。

entries.definition: A running store that holds and queries many records; a dataset is usually one prepared collection taken from such stores.
entries.definitionCN: 保存并查询大量记录的运行系统；dataset 通常是从这类库中取出的一份准备好的集合。

entries.definition: A short document listing the specifications of a product; it describes equipment, not research records.
entries.definitionCN: 列出一件产品规格的短文档；它描述设备，不描述研究记录。

entries.definition: A set contained within a larger one; a subset of a dataset is still a dataset only when handled as a unit.
entries.definitionCN: 包含在更大集合里的集合；数据集的一部分只有在被整体处理时才仍叫数据集。

entries.definition: A body of texts assembled for linguistic study; a dataset may hold numbers, images or texts, so corpus is narrower.
entries.definitionCN: 为语言研究汇编的文本总体；dataset 可含数字、图像或文本，corpus 更窄。

entries.definition: A part chosen to represent a whole; a dataset may be a complete collection rather than a sample.
entries.definitionCN: 为代表整体而选出的部分；dataset 可能是完整集合，而不只是样本。

entries.definition: Any group of gathered items; dataset adds the expectation of records meant for analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 任何收集起来的一组物品；dataset 多了「供分析用的记录」这一预期。

entries.definition: Data arranged in rows and columns; many datasets are tables, but a dataset can also be images or text.
entries.definitionCN: 按行列排列的数据；许多数据集是表，但数据集也可以是图像或文本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real two halves, the real statistical history and the real modelling phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的两个构件、真实的统计史与真实的建模搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Data plus set: a set is a group counted as one, so a dataset is data handled as one thing.
normal.cn: data 加 set：集合是被当作一个来数的组，所以数据集就是被当成一件东西处理的数据。

normal.en: The family runs data, dataset, database, subset and metadata.
normal.cn: 同族词有 data、dataset、database、subset 与 metadata。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the modelling roles: training dataset, test dataset, benchmark dataset.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出建模角色：训练数据集、测试数据集、基准数据集。

normal.en: Statisticians used data set before computers, so the word is not originally a computing term.
normal.cn: 统计学家在计算机之前就用 data set，所以这个词原本不是计算机术语。

normal.en: A database runs and answers queries; a dataset is a fixed collection you can hand to someone.
normal.cn: database 运行并回答查询；dataset 是可以交到别人手里的固定集合。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of forms that knows exactly how many rows it has.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠表格，清楚知道自己有多少行。

abstract.en: Picture a bucket of observations poured out one row at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一桶观测，一次倒出一行。

abstract.en: Picture a name tag pinned to a pile of numbers so it can be cited.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆数字被别上名牌，于是可以被引用。

examples.en: The dataset contains images labelled by three independent raters.
examples.cn: 这份数据集包含由三位独立评分者标注的图像。

examples.en: They split the dataset into training and test halves.
examples.cn: 他们把数据集分成训练与测试两半。

examples.en: A dataset without documentation is hard to reuse.
examples.cn: 没有说明文档的数据集很难复用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「得（da）他（ta）赛（set）」——得到他那套比赛用的材料，就是数据集

root: 拉丁 dare「给予」→ datum → 复数 data「数据」；上古英语 settan「放置」→ 名词 set「一组」；data 与 set 合为 dataset。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the collection from a plain unit of records to a model input, a benchmark, survey observations, a published artifact, one split, a structured file and a citable repository item.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着「集合」走：从素朴的记录单位，到模型输入、基准、调查观测、公开发布物、某一划分、结构化文件，再到可引用的仓库条目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of tidy tables on a long desk, one record per row, one field per column.
core.cn: 核心意象：长桌上一叠整齐的表格，每行一条记录，每列一个字段。

branches.en: ONE UNIT: related records grouped so they can be moved and described together.
branches.cn: 一个单位：相关记录归在一起，可以整体搬运与描述。

branches.en: MODELLING: one body to train on, and one part held back to test.
branches.cn: 建模：一份用来训练，一份留作测试。

branches.en: SHARED REFERENCE: a benchmark everyone scores on, released openly and citable.
branches.cn: 共享参照：人人都在上面打分的基准，公开释放且可引用。

branches.en: OBSERVATION: the records a survey or experiment actually gathered.
branches.cn: 观测：调查或实验实际收集到的记录。

branches.en: OBJECT WITH STRUCTURE AND NAME: schema and identifier turn rows into a reusable artifact.
branches.cn: 有结构有名字的对象：结构说明与标识把行变成可复用的成果。

intro.en: Dataset joins a Latin-derived plural to a native English noun; neither half carries an affix, and the compound is held together by English word order.
intro.cn: dataset 把一个拉丁来源的复数与一个英语本族名词接在一起；两半都不带词缀，复合靠英语词序维系。

latinIntro.en: Only data is Latin; set is native English. There is no Latin compound behind dataset, which is why its structure is so transparent.
latinIntro.cn: 只有 data 来自拉丁语；set 是英语本族词。dataset 背后没有拉丁复合词，所以结构才这么透明。

items.example: The verb explains why data are called given.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词解释了数据为什么被称为「被给予的」。

items.example: One observation is one datum.
items.exampleCN: 一条观测就是一个数据点。

items.example: The plural became an English mass noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个复数成了英语的不可数名词。

items.example: The verb is the root of the noun set.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词 set 的词根。

items.example: A set counts as one.
items.exampleCN: 一个集合被算作一个。

items.example: The compound names a portable collection.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指可搬运的集合。

items.meaning: a set inside a larger set
items.meaningCN: 包含在更大集合中的集合
items.example: A subset is still made of records.
items.exampleCN: 子集仍然由记录构成。

items.example: Metadata describes the columns of a dataset.
items.exampleCN: 元数据描述数据集的各列。

items.example: The bank image stresses storage rather than size.
items.exampleCN: bank 的意象强调存储而非规模。

definition_en: the systematic conversion of raw data into usable information by a defined procedure
core_image: 一筐杂乱的单据倒进机器，出来时变成整齐的汇总表
scene: 一筐杂乱的单据被倒进机器入口，出来时已变成整齐的汇总表，边角还盖着日期戳。The office moved its data processing to a shared service so that bills were checked overnight.
sceneCN: 这里 data processing 指把原始数据按固定流程转换成可用信息的工作（第 1 个义项：把原始数据转成可用信息）；句意：办公室把数据处理移交给共享服务，账单因而能在一夜之间核对完毕。图中可辨识物件：单据筐、机器入口、汇总表、日期戳。

senses.title: Turning raw data into information
senses.definition: the work of sorting, calculating and summarizing raw records so that they become useful
senses.definitionCN: 对原始记录进行排序、计算与汇总，使它们变得有用的工作
senses.example: Data processing turns a pile of receipts into a monthly total.
senses.exampleCN: 数据处理把一堆收据变成月度总额。
senses.why: the phrase names a transformation rather than a tool: raw records go in, usable information comes out.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语命名的是一次转换而非一件工具：原料记录进去，可用信息出来。

senses.title: Processing done by computer
senses.definition: the same work carried out automatically by electronic machines
senses.definitionCN: 由电子机器自动完成的同一类工作
senses.example: Electronic data processing replaced rooms full of clerks.
senses.exampleCN: 电子数据处理取代了成屋子的办事员。
senses.why: when machines took over the work, the phrase kept its meaning and gained an adjective rather than a new noun.
senses.whyCN: 机器接管这项工作后，短语保留原义，只加了一个形容词，而没有另造名词。

senses.title: Batch processing of transactions
senses.definition: collecting transactions and running them through the system in one scheduled pass
senses.definitionCN: 收集事务并在一次排定的运行中统一处理
senses.example: Payroll data processing runs as a batch every second Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 工资数据处理每隔一个周五成批运行一次。
senses.why: early machines were fastest when fed work in large blocks, and that style became a named sense of the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 早期机器在大批喂入任务时最快，这种做法就成了短语的一个具名义项。

senses.title: Routine business processing
senses.definition: the regular handling of invoices, payroll, stock and accounts in an organization
senses.definitionCN: 组织中发票、工资、库存与账目的常规处理
senses.example: The accounts data processing team closes the books each month.
senses.exampleCN: 账务数据处理团队每月结账。
senses.why: business administration adopted the phrase for its recurring paperwork long before computers, and kept it afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 商务管理远在计算机之前就用这个短语指重复性的单据工作，此后一直沿用。

senses.title: Entry, validation and cleaning
senses.definition: the front-end work of keying data in, checking formats and removing errors
senses.definitionCN: 录入数据、检查格式并剔除错误的前端工作
senses.example: Most data processing errors come from the entry step, not the report.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数数据处理错误来自录入环节，而不是报表。
senses.why: before any calculation can be trusted, records must be made consistent, and that preparation belongs under the same phrase.
senses.whyCN: 在计算结果可信之前，记录必须先一致，这份准备工作也算在同一个短语之下。

senses.title: Scientific and statistical processing
senses.definition: the preparation and analysis of measurements from experiments or surveys
senses.definitionCN: 对实验或调查所得测量的整理与分析
senses.example: Satellite data processing removes noise before the images are studied.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星数据处理在图像被研究之前先去掉噪声。
senses.why: research produces raw measurements that must be corrected and summarized, which is the same transformation under another domain.
senses.whyCN: 研究产出的原始测量必须被校正与汇总，这是同一转换在另一个领域里的表现。

senses.title: Processing personal data under law
senses.definition: any operation performed on personal information, as defined by privacy law
senses.definitionCN: 隐私法所定义的、对个人信息进行的任何操作
senses.example: The contract sets out what data processing the supplier may perform.
senses.exampleCN: 合同列明供应商可进行哪些数据处理。
senses.why: privacy law needed a broad term covering collection, storage and deletion, and chose this everyday phrase.
senses.whyCN: 隐私法需要一个涵盖收集、存储与删除的宽泛术语，于是选用了这个日常短语。

senses.title: Manual and clerical processing
senses.definition: the same work done by hand, with files, ledgers and written rules
senses.definitionCN: 用档案、账簿与书面规则手工完成的同类工作
senses.example: Before the machines, data processing meant clerks and filing cabinets.
senses.exampleCN: 在有机器之前，数据处理意味着办事员与档案柜。
senses.why: the phrase never required a computer, so it still describes paper-based work in small offices and archives.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语从来不要求计算机，因此仍可描述小办公室与档案馆里的纸面工作。

intro.en: Data processing joins data, the plural of Latin datum, to processing, from Latin procedere by way of process. The phrase is twentieth-century, though the work is older. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: data processing 把拉丁语 datum 的复数 data 与出自拉丁语 procedere 的 processing 接在一起。短语是二十世纪的，但这项工作更老。年代均为约数。

items.en: Datum means something given, from dare, to give; the plural data entered English as a mass of facts to be handled.
items.cn: datum 意为「被给予的东西」，出自 dare「给予」；复数 data 以「待处理的大量事实」之意进入英语。

items.en: Procedere is pro-, forward, plus cedere, to go: to go forward, hence to advance a matter through stages.
items.cn: procedere 是 pro-「向前」加 cedere「走」：向前走，引申为把事情分阶段推进。

items.en: Latin processus, a going forward, gave English process, which as a verb means to put material through a series of operations.
items.cn: 拉丁语 processus「前进」给出英语 process，作动词时指把材料送过一连串操作。

items.en: Data processing became common in the mid-twentieth century for the clerical and then electronic handling of records in offices.
items.cn: data processing 在二十世纪中期通行起来，先指办公室里的文书记录处理，后指电子处理。

items.en: Electronic data processing named a whole industry and a job title, and the phrase survived the move from punched cards to networks.
items.cn: 电子数据处理曾是一个行业与一个职位的名称，短语也从穿孔卡时代活到了网络时代。

items.en: The first half from Latin datum and the second from Latin procedere are both documented. The phrase's first use is dated only approximately, and any older Indo-European source for cedere or dare is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：前半出自拉丁语 datum，后半出自拉丁语 procedere，两段都有文献依据；短语最早使用的年代只有约数，cedere 与 dare 更早的印欧语来源属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is the phrase's own parts and near forms; the second group names neighbouring activities that handle data.
note.cn: 第一组是短语自身的构件与近形；第二组是同样与数据打交道的相邻活动。

entries.definition: Putting material through a series of operations; alone it could refer to food or applications, not only data.
entries.definitionCN: 把材料送过一连串操作；单独用时也可指食品或申请，不只数据。

entries.definition: The one that performs the processing, whether a clerk, a service or a chip; the phrase names the work, not the worker.
entries.definitionCN: 执行处理的一方，可以是办事员、服务或芯片；短语指工作，不指执行者。

entries.definition: The raw records before any operation; processing is what makes them useful.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未经过任何操作的原始记录；处理才使它们有用。

entries.definition: The part of a computer that executes instructions; it is hardware, whereas data processing is the work done with it.
entries.definitionCN: 计算机中执行指令的部件；它是硬件，而数据处理是用它完成的工作。

entries.definition: Looking for patterns and meaning; processing prepares and transforms records, analysis asks what they show.
entries.definitionCN: 寻找模式与含义；processing 负责准备与转换记录，analysis 追问它们说明什么。

entries.definition: The single step of typing records into a system; it is one part of data processing, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 把记录敲入系统的单一步骤；它是数据处理的一部分，而非全部。

entries.definition: A broader phrase covering any transformation of information, including by minds; data processing usually implies records and machines or clerks.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽的短语，涵盖任何信息转换，包括由头脑完成；data processing 通常暗示记录与机器或办事员。

entries.definition: Working out results by arithmetic or logic; data processing includes sorting and formatting, which are not computation.
entries.definitionCN: 用算术或逻辑算出结果；数据处理还包括排序与排版，那些不算计算。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin pieces, the real office history and the real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁构件、真实的办公史与真实的固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Data are the raw facts; processing is putting them through steps until they are useful.
normal.cn: data 是原始事实；processing 是让它们过一遍步骤直到有用。

normal.en: Procedere is pro- forward plus cedere go, so a process is a going forward through stages.
normal.cn: procedere 是 pro-「向前」加 cedere「走」，所以 process 就是分阶段向前推进。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the office world: data processing system, data processing department, batch processing.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出办公世界：数据处理系统、数据处理部门、批处理。

normal.en: The family runs data, process, processing, processor and data processor.
normal.cn: 同族词有 data、process、processing、processor 与 data processor。

normal.en: Privacy law uses the phrase for any operation on personal information, including deletion.
normal.cn: 隐私法用这个短语指对个人信息的任何操作，包括删除。

abstract.en: Picture a basket of receipts entering a machine and leaving as one clean total.
abstract.cn: 想象一筐收据进入机器，出来时成了一个干净的总数。

abstract.en: Picture a river of paper narrowing into a single tap.
abstract.cn: 想象一条纸的河流收窄成一个水龙头。

abstract.en: Picture clerks handing their ledgers to a humming box that never sleeps.
abstract.cn: 想象办事员把账簿交给一只嗡嗡作响、从不睡觉的盒子。

examples.en: The department handles data processing for every regional office.
examples.cn: 这个部门为所有地区办公室做数据处理。

examples.en: Good data processing catches a wrong date before it reaches the report.
examples.cn: 好的数据处理能在错误日期进入报表之前把它抓住。

examples.en: The contract limits how much personal data processing the vendor may do.
examples.cn: 合同限制了供应商可进行多少个人数据处理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「得（da）他（ta）＋剥（pro）塞（cess）ing」——把得到的数据一层层剥开塞进流程，就是数据处理

root: 拉丁 dare「给予」→ datum → 复数 data「数据」；拉丁 pro-「向前」+ cedere「走」→ procedere → processus → process「处理」；processing 为 process 的动名词，二者合为 data processing。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one transformation from raw records to usable information, then branch into machine work, batch runs, office routine, entry work, research, legal definition and plain clerical handling.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一次转换展开：从原始记录到可用信息，再分叉到机器处理、成批运行、办公例行、录入工作、科研、法律定义与纯文书处理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a basket of messy slips tipped into a machine and coming out as a clean summary sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一筐杂乱单据倒进机器，出来时是一张干净的汇总表。

branches.en: TRANSFORMATION: sorting, calculating and summarizing until records become information.
branches.cn: 转换：排序、计算与汇总，直到记录变成信息。

branches.en: MACHINE STYLE: the same work done by electronics, often in scheduled blocks.
branches.cn: 机器方式：同一工作由电子设备完成，常按排定的批次进行。

branches.en: OFFICE ROUTINE: invoices, payroll and accounts processed on a repeating cycle.
branches.cn: 办公例行：发票、工资与账目按循环周期处理。

branches.en: PREPARATION: entry, validation and cleaning come before any trusted result.
branches.cn: 准备：录入、校验与清洗先于任何可信结果。

branches.en: DOMAINS: science, privacy law and paper-based clerks all use the same phrase for their own handling of records.
branches.cn: 领域：科研、隐私法与纸面办事员都用同一个短语指各自对记录的处理。

intro.en: The phrase is two Latin-derived elements: data from dare through datum, and processing from procedere through process plus the English ending -ing.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个拉丁来源成分构成：data 出自 dare 经 datum，processing 出自 procedere 经 process 再加英语词尾 -ing。

latinIntro.en: Latin gives datum and procedere; the ending -ing that makes the second half a noun is English, added after process had already entered the language.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语给出 datum 与 procedere；把后半变成名词的 -ing 是英语词尾，是在 process 已进入英语之后才加上去的。

items.example: Data are literally the given.
items.exampleCN: 数据字面上就是被给予的东西。

items.example: A datum is one recorded fact.
items.exampleCN: 一个数据点就是一条记录事实。

items.example: The plural now works as a mass noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个复数如今作不可数名词用。

items.example: The verb supplies the movement inside process.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 process 里的「行进」意味。

items.example: A matter is advanced through stages.
items.exampleCN: 事情被分阶段向前推进。

items.example: The noun became English process.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词成了英语 process。

items.example: The verb is the working core of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是短语的工作核心。

items.example: Processing names the activity rather than one run.
items.exampleCN: processing 指这项活动，而不是某一次运行。

items.example: The gerund can be uncountable.
items.exampleCN: 这个动名词可以不可数。

items.example: Processor names the machine or the person.
items.exampleCN: processor 指机器或人。

definition_en: the field, systems and industry concerned with using computers and networks to store, process and transmit information
core_image: 办公室里一面流程图，桌上一排显示器，墙角文件柜与服务器指示灯同时亮着
scene: 办公室里挂着一面流程图，桌上一排显示器，墙角的文件柜与服务器指示灯同时亮着。The firm hired an information technology team to move its records off paper.
sceneCN: 这里 information technology 指用计算机与网络处理信息的整个领域（第 1 个义项：用计算机与网络存储、处理、传输信息的领域）；句意：这家公司雇了一支信息技术团队，把记录从纸面搬走。图中可辨识物件：流程图、显示器、文件柜、服务器指示灯。

senses.title: The field of applying computers to information
senses.titleCN: 用计算机处理信息的领域
senses.definition: the study and practice of using computers, networks and software to store, process and send information
senses.definitionCN: 研究并实践用计算机、网络与软件存储、处理与传送信息
senses.example: Information technology now underpins almost every office task.
senses.exampleCN: 信息技术如今支撑着几乎每一项办公任务。
senses.why: the phrase names a field by its object, information, and its means, technology; together they mark the systematic use of machines on information.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语用对象「信息」与手段「技术」来命名一个领域；两者合起来指系统地用机器处理信息。

senses.title: The industry and sector
senses.definition: the business sector that sells hardware, software, networks and support
senses.definitionCN: 出售硬件、软件、网络与支持服务的商业部门
senses.example: Information technology is one of the region's largest employers.
senses.exampleCN: 信息技术是该地区最大的雇主之一。
senses.why: a field with paid specialists becomes an industry, and the phrase then names the trade as well as the knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 一个有报酬专家的领域会变成产业，短语于是既指知识，也指这门行当。

senses.title: An organization's IT department
senses.titleCN: 组织内的信息技术部门
senses.definition: the internal unit responsible for an organization's computers and systems
senses.definitionCN: 组织中负责计算机与系统的内部单位
senses.example: Information technology moved the whole staff onto one network.
senses.exampleCN: 信息技术部门把全体员工迁到了同一个网络上。
senses.why: institutions name the unit after the field it manages, so the phrase also means a desk or a floor within a company.
senses.whyCN: 机构按所管理的领域给部门命名，因此短语也指公司里的某个工位或某层楼。

senses.title: The systems and equipment
senses.definition: the computers, servers, networks and software considered as one infrastructure
senses.definitionCN: 把计算机、服务器、网络与软件视为一套基础设施
senses.example: The old information technology was replaced over one weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 旧的信息技术设备在一个周末内被换掉。
senses.why: users say the technology when they mean the installed equipment, because the equipment is the visible body of the field.
senses.whyCN: 使用者说「这项技术」时其实指装好的设备，因为设备是这个领域可见的躯体。

senses.title: A school or degree subject
senses.definition: a course of study teaching computing and information systems
senses.definitionCN: 教授计算与信息系统的课程
senses.example: She took information technology as her second subject.
senses.exampleCN: 她把信息技术选为第二科目。
senses.why: once the field had a body of knowledge, schools packaged it as a subject with the same name.
senses.whyCN: 领域一旦拥有知识体系，学校就把它打包成同名科目。

senses.title: The support function
senses.definition: the help desk and maintenance work that keeps systems running
senses.definitionCN: 使系统持续运行的帮助台与维护工作
senses.example: Information technology answered the ticket within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 信息技术支持在一小时内回复了工单。
senses.why: much of the field's daily work is repair and support, and the phrase covers that service as well as design.
senses.whyCN: 这个领域的大量日常工作是维修与支持，短语因此也涵盖服务，而不只是设计。

senses.title: Policy and governance
senses.definition: the rules and oversight that decide how systems and data may be used
senses.definitionCN: 决定系统与数据可如何使用的规则与监督
senses.example: Information technology policy forbids storing client data on laptops.
senses.exampleCN: 信息技术政策禁止在笔记本电脑上存放客户数据。
senses.why: as systems became critical, the phrase gained a governance sense: not the machines but the rules around them.
senses.whyCN: 系统一旦变得关键，短语就多了治理义：不是机器本身，而是围绕机器的规则。

senses.title: Practical computer skills
senses.definition: used loosely for the everyday ability to use computers and common software
senses.definitionCN: 宽泛指使用计算机与常用软件的日常能力
senses.example: Basic information technology skills are now expected of every clerk.
senses.exampleCN: 如今每个办事员都被要求具备基本的信息技术技能。
senses.why: employers shortened a grand field name into a line on a job advert, meaning simply that a person can use the tools.
senses.whyCN: 雇主把宏大的领域名缩成招聘广告上的一行，意思只是「会用这些工具」。

intro.en: Information technology joins information, from Latin informatio, to technology, from Greek technē plus -logia. The full phrase is a mid-twentieth-century coinage; the abbreviation IT spread later. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: information technology 把出自拉丁语 informatio 的 information 与出自希腊语 technē 加 -logia 的 technology 接在一起。完整短语是二十世纪中期的产物；缩写 IT 更晚流行。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin informatio meant a sketch, an outline or a shaping, from informare, to give form to something. English information shifted from instruction to facts communicated.
items.cn: 拉丁语 informatio 指草图、纲要或塑形，出自 informare「赋予形状」。英语 information 从「教导」转向「被传达的事实」。

items.en: Greek technē meant craft, skill or a trained art, and it covered both making things and the knowledge behind making them.
items.cn: 希腊语 technē 指手艺、技能或有训练的艺术，既涵盖制造，也涵盖制造背后的知识。

items.en: The ending -logia, from logos, gave names to systematic studies; technology first meant the study of the practical arts before it meant the arts themselves.
items.cn: 出自 logos 的词尾 -logia 为系统研究命名；technology 最初指对实用技艺的研究，后来才指技艺本身。

items.en: Information technology appeared in the mid-twentieth century, when computing and communications began to be discussed as one combined field.
items.cn: information technology 在二十世纪中期出现，当时计算与通信开始被当作一个合并领域来讨论。

items.en: The short form IT became ordinary in the 1970s and 1980s as offices installed their own machines and departments were named after them.
items.cn: 缩写 IT 在 1970 至 1980 年代变得普通，因为办公室装上了自己的机器，部门也以它命名。

items.en: The first half from Latin informatio and the second from Greek technē plus -logia are both documented. The full phrase is dated to the mid-twentieth century only approximately, and any older Indo-European source for technē is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：前半出自拉丁语 informatio，后半出自希腊语 technē 加 -logia，两段都有文献依据；完整短语最早出现的年代只有约数，technē 更早的印欧语来源属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is the phrase's own halves and its abbreviation; the second group names neighbouring fields and wider labels.
note.cn: 第一组是短语自身两半及其缩写；第二组是相邻领域与更宽的标签。

entries.definition: The two-letter abbreviation of information technology; it is informal and usually refers to the department or the field, not to one device.
entries.definitionCN: information technology 的两个字母缩写；偏口语，通常指部门或领域，不指单台设备。

entries.definition: Facts and messages considered as content; the phrase names the technology that handles this content.
entries.definitionCN: 被当作内容看待的事实与消息；短语指处理这类内容的技术。

entries.definition: Applied knowledge and its tools; alone it covers bridges and looms as much as computers.
entries.definitionCN: 应用知识及其工具；单独使用时也可指桥梁与织机，不只计算机。

entries.definition: One organized system for collecting and using information; information technology is the wider field and infrastructure that support many such systems.
entries.definitionCN: 一套收集与使用信息的组织化系统；information technology 是支撑许多这类系统的更宽领域与基础设施。

entries.definition: The use and study of computers; it stresses calculation and machines, while information technology stresses information and services.
entries.definitionCN: 计算机的使用与研究；它强调计算与机器，information technology 强调信息与服务。

entries.definition: Information and communication technology, a wider label that adds networks and telephony to the same field.
entries.definitionCN: 信息与通信技术，是更宽的标签，在同一领域里加入网络与电话。

entries.definition: The science of information processing and systems; it is more academic, while information technology is more applied and operational.
entries.definitionCN: 研究信息处理与系统的科学；更偏学术，而 information technology 更偏应用与运维。

entries.definition: Technology that works with discrete numeric signals; it describes the means, while information technology describes the purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 以离散数字信号工作的技术；它描述手段，information technology 描述目的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin and Greek pieces, the real departmental life and the real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁与希腊构件、真实的部门生活与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Information is what is handled; technology is how it is handled; together they name the field.
normal.cn: 信息是处理的内容，技术是处理的手段，合起来就是一个领域。

normal.en: The family runs information, technology, technological, technologist and IT.
normal.cn: 同族词有 information、technology、technological、technologist 与 IT。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the workplace: information technology department, services, infrastructure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出职场：信息技术部门、服务、基础设施。

normal.en: Latin informare means to give form, so information is content that has been shaped.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 informare 意为赋予形状，所以信息是被塑过形的内容。

normal.en: Greek technē means craft, so technology began as the study of crafts before it meant the tools.
normal.cn: 希腊语 technē 意为手艺，所以 technology 最初指对手艺的研究，后来才指工具。

abstract.en: Picture a filing cabinet and a server rack breathing in the same room.
abstract.cn: 想象一只文件柜与一台服务器在同一间屋里一起呼吸。

abstract.en: Picture a paper form dissolving into a screen without anyone touching it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸质表格无人触碰就溶进屏幕。

abstract.en: Picture a department whose only product is things continuing to work.
abstract.cn: 想象一个部门，它唯一的产品就是「东西继续能用」。

examples.en: Information technology budgets are now larger than property budgets in many firms.
examples.cn: 许多公司里信息技术预算已超过房产预算。

examples.en: The information technology team trained staff before the new system went live.
examples.cn: 信息技术团队在新系统上线前培训了员工。

examples.en: She studied information technology before moving into design.
examples.cn: 她在转向设计之前学的是信息技术。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因（in）佛（for）没（me）神（tion）＋太（tech）可（no）了（lo）机（gy）」——把信息交给机器打理的那套技术

root: 拉丁 informare「赋予形状」→ informatio「纲要、塑形」→ 英语 information「信息」；希腊 technē「手艺」+ -logia「学问」→ 英语 technology「技术」；两词合为 information technology。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a field of study to an industry, an internal department, installed equipment, a school subject, a support desk, a body of policy and finally a line on a job advert.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从研究领域走到产业、内部部门、装好的设备、学校科目、支持台、政策体系，最后走到招聘广告上的一行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flowchart on the wall, monitors on the desk and a server light blinking beside an old filing cabinet.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上的流程图、桌上的显示器，以及旧文件柜旁闪烁的服务器指示灯。

branches.en: FIELD: computers and networks applied systematically to information.
branches.cn: 领域：计算机与网络被系统地用于信息。

branches.en: ORGANIZATION: the trade that sells the work, and the unit inside a firm that performs it.
branches.cn: 组织：出售这项工作的行业，以及公司内部执行它的单位。

branches.en: MACHINES AND SERVICE: the installed infrastructure, and the support that keeps it alive.
branches.cn: 机器与服务：装好的基础设施，以及使它存活的支撑。

branches.en: SUBJECT: a body of knowledge packaged for teaching and degrees.
branches.cn: 科目：为教学与学位打包好的知识体系。

branches.en: RULES AND SKILLS: governance above the systems, and the everyday ability expected below them.
branches.cn: 规则与技能：系统之上的治理，以及系统之下被要求的日常能力。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin noun to a Greek-derived noun: information from informare, technology from technē plus -logia.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个拉丁名词与一个希腊来源名词接在一起：information 出自 informare，technology 出自 technē 加 -logia。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies forma, informare and informatio for the first half; technē and logos are Greek and reached English through Latinised learning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语为前半提供 forma、informare 与 informatio；technē 与 logos 是希腊语，经拉丁化学术传统进入英语。

items.example: The noun supplies the image of something shaped.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供「被塑成形」的意象。

items.example: To inform is literally to put a shape into something.
items.exampleCN: inform 字面上就是往某物里放入一个形状。

items.example: The Latin noun became English information.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词成了英语 information。

items.example: The first half names what is handled.
items.exampleCN: 前半命名被处理的内容。

items.example: The Greek noun covers both making and knowing how.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词同时涵盖制造与懂得怎么制造。

items.example: The ending built names for systematic studies.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成了系统研究的名。

items.meaning: the study and then the tools of craft
items.meaningCN: 先是技艺之学，后指技艺工具
items.example: The sense shifted from knowledge to equipment.
items.exampleCN: 词义从知识转向设备。

items.example: Technical writing explains how something is done.
items.exampleCN: 技术写作解释某事怎么做。

items.example: The adjective marks the means rather than the purpose.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标出手段而非目的。

items.example: The abbreviation became a department name.
items.exampleCN: 这个缩写成了部门名。

definition_zh: 数字的；用数字表示的；数字技术的；手指的
definition_en: expressed in discrete numbers, using computer technology, or relating to a finger
core_image: 一块显示屏上，连续的曲线被切成一根根竖直的柱子，柱顶连成折线
scene: 屏幕上原本平滑的曲线被切成一根根竖直的柱子，柱顶连成折线，每个柱高都对应一个整数。The studio moved its archive from tape to a digital format last year.
sceneCN: 这里 digital 指以离散数字表示声音或图像的（第 2 个义项：用离散数值表示的）；句意：工作室去年把档案从磁带转成了数字格式。图中可辨识物件：屏幕、竖柱、折线、整数刻度。

pos.zh: 数字的；数字技术的；手指的

senses.title: Relating to fingers
senses.definition: belonging to a finger or toe in anatomy
senses.definitionCN: 解剖学上属于手指或脚趾的
senses.example: The digital artery supplies the tip of the finger.
senses.exampleCN: 指动脉为指尖供血。
senses.why: the oldest sense comes straight from Latin digitus, a finger, and survives mainly in medical description.
senses.whyCN: 最老的意思直接来自拉丁语 digitus「手指」，主要活在医学描述里。

senses.title: Expressed as discrete numbers
senses.definition: represented by separate numbered steps rather than a continuous range
senses.definitionCN: 用一个个分开的编号取值表示，而非连续区间
senses.example: A digital signal stores only the sampled values, not the curve between them.
senses.exampleCN: 数字信号只保存采样值，不保存值之间的曲线。
senses.why: counting on fingers produced the word digit for a numeral, and digital came to mean working in those separate units.
senses.whyCN: 用手指计数产生了表示数字的 digit，digital 于是指以这些分离单位运作。

senses.title: Using computer technology
senses.definition: involving computers, networks or software rather than mechanical or paper means
senses.definitionCN: 涉及计算机、网络或软件，而非机械或纸面手段
senses.example: The library offers digital versions of every journal it holds.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆提供馆藏每种期刊的数字版本。
senses.why: since computers store everything as discrete numbers, the adjective became the everyday label for computer-based media.
senses.whyCN: 由于计算机把一切存成离散数字，这个形容词成了计算机媒介的日常标签。

senses.title: Showing a numeric readout
senses.definition: describing a device that shows figures rather than a moving pointer
senses.definitionCN: 指用数字显示而非指针移动来读数的设备
senses.example: The digital clock in the hall lost a minute overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅里的数字钟一夜之间慢了一分钟。
senses.why: a numeric display replaces a continuous dial with countable steps, which is the same distinction in a small object.
senses.whyCN: 数字显示用可数的台阶取代连续表盘，这是同一种区分在小物件上的体现。

senses.title: Belonging to online media
senses.definition: describing content, markets or habits that exist mainly through digital networks
senses.definitionCN: 指主要经由数字网络存在的内容、市场或习惯
senses.example: Digital audiences now outnumber print subscribers.
senses.exampleCN: 数字受众如今超过了纸质订阅者。
senses.why: the adjective spread from the signal to the whole social world built on it, such as digital markets and digital literacy.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从信号扩散到建立在信号之上的整个社会世界，如数字市场与数字素养。

senses.title: Of a digital circuit
senses.definition: describing circuits that work with two levels, on and off, rather than a range
senses.definitionCN: 指只处理开与关两个电平、而非连续范围的电路
senses.example: A digital circuit ignores small voltage fluctuations.
senses.exampleCN: 数字电路忽略微小的电压波动。
senses.why: engineering needed a word for the two-level style of design, and reused the adjective already attached to discrete values.
senses.whyCN: 工程需要给这种双电平设计方式一个词，于是复用了已表示离散取值的形容词。

senses.title: Produced by numeric recording
senses.definition: describing sound or images captured and stored as numeric samples
senses.definitionCN: 指以数字采样录制与保存的声音或图像
senses.example: Digital recordings survive copying better than tape.
senses.exampleCN: 数字录音比磁带更耐复制。
senses.why: copies of numbers are exact, so recorded media were the first consumer product to be sold on this adjective.
senses.whyCN: 数字的副本是精确的，因此录音媒介成了最早以这个形容词出售的消费品。

senses.title: Of electronic money and records
senses.definition: describing payments, signatures or records that exist only as data
senses.definitionCN: 指只以数据形式存在的支付、签名或记录
senses.example: A digital signature can be checked without a paper original.
senses.exampleCN: 数字签名无需纸质原件就能核验。
senses.why: once trust moved into data, the adjective named the whole class of transactions with no physical body.
senses.whyCN: 一旦信任迁入数据，这个形容词就命名了整类没有实体的交易。

senses.title: Contrasted with analog
senses.definition: forming one half of the technical pair digital and analog
senses.definitionCN: 构成「数字」与「模拟」这对技术对立的一半
senses.example: Engineers compare digital and analog designs by cost, not by age.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师按成本而非新旧来比较数字与模拟设计。
senses.why: the adjective's clearest job is to mark one side of a binary contrast, and that contrast organizes whole industries.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词最清晰的作用是标出一组二分对立的一边，而这组对立组织了整个行业。

intro.en: Digital comes from Latin digitus, a finger, through digitalis, of a finger. The numeral sense grew from counting on fingers, and the electronic sense is a twentieth-century extension. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: digital 出自拉丁语 digitus「手指」，经 digitalis「手指的」而来。数字义由用手指计数生长出来，电子义是二十世纪的延伸。年代均为约数。

items.en: Digitus meant a finger or a toe. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the word is not built from an obvious root in Latin.
items.cn: digitus 指手指或脚趾。它更早的来源不确定；这个词并非由拉丁语中某个显而易见的词根构成。

items.en: The adjective digitalis meant belonging to a finger, and English took it as digital in the fifteenth century for matters of fingers.
items.cn: 形容词 digitalis 意为「属于手指的」，英语在十五世纪以 digital 接收它，指与手指相关的事。

items.en: Because people count on their fingers, digit came to mean any of the numerals nought to nine, and digital followed into the sense of working with numerals.
items.cn: 因为人用手指计数，digit 引申为从零到九的任一数字，digital 也随之进入「用数字运作」这一义。

items.en: In the twentieth century digital described clocks and meters that show figures instead of a moving pointer.
items.cn: 二十世纪时，digital 描述用数字而非移动指针显示的钟表与仪表。

items.en: From the 1940s digital named machines that compute with discrete states, and then the media, markets and records built on them.
items.cn: 自 1940 年代起，digital 指以离散状态计算的机器，随后又指建立在它们之上的媒介、市场与记录。

items.en: The chain from Latin digitus through digitalis to English digital is documented. The origin of digitus before Latin is not settled and the comparisons offered for it are reconstructions; the earliest dates of the numeral and computing senses are also approximate.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：从拉丁语 digitus 经 digitalis 到该词的链条有文献依据；digitus 本身在拉丁语之前的来源尚无定论，为它提出的比较属于重构形式；数字义与电子义的最早年代同样只有约数。

note.en: The first group shares the digit stem and is easily confused; the second group names neighbouring descriptions of computed and electronic things.
note.cn: 第一组共享 digit 词干，容易混淆；第二组是描述计算与电子事物的相邻说法。

entries.definition: A numeral from nought to nine, or a finger; digital is the adjective built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指零到九的一个数字，或一根手指；digital 是由它构成的形容词。

entries.definition: By digital means; it answers how something is done, while digital answers what kind it is.
entries.definitionCN: 以数字方式；副词回答「怎样做」，digital 回答「哪一类」。

entries.definition: To convert into digital form; the verb names the act, the adjective names the result's kind.
entries.definitionCN: 转换成数字形式；动词指动作，形容词指结果的类别。

entries.definition: The process of converting analog material into digital form; narrower than digitalization, which can mean wider organizational change.
entries.definitionCN: 把模拟材料转成数字形式的过程；比 digitalization 窄，后者可指更广的组织变革。

entries.definition: Relating to numbers as values; digital adds the sense of discrete representation or computer technology.
entries.definitionCN: 与作为数值的数字有关；digital 多了「离散表示」或「计算机技术」的意思。

entries.definition: Working by means of electronic circuits; digital describes the form of the information, electronic describes the hardware that carries it.
entries.definitionCN: 以电子电路运作；digital 描述信息的形式，electronic 描述承载它的硬件。

entries.definition: Converted to computer control; it describes a change of system, while digital can describe the data itself.
entries.definitionCN: 转为计算机控制；它描述系统的更换，digital 可描述数据本身。

entries.definition: Connected to a network; online content is usually digital, but digital content need not be online.
entries.definitionCN: 接入网络；线上内容通常是数字的，但数字内容不必在线。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin word for finger, the real counting link and the real phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「手指」词、真实的计数联系与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Digitus is Latin for finger: people counted on fingers, so a numeral became a digit and its adjective became digital.
normal.cn: digitus 是拉丁语「手指」：人用手指计数，于是数字成了 digit，其形容词成了 digital。

normal.en: The family runs digit, digital, digitally, digitize and digitization.
normal.cn: 同族词有 digit、digital、digitally、digitize 与 digitization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the modern sense: digital signal, digital archive, digital economy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出现代义：数字信号、数字档案、数字经济。

normal.en: The medical sense survives: a digital artery is an artery of the finger, not a computer artery.
normal.cn: 医学义仍活着：指动脉是手指的动脉，不是计算机的动脉。

normal.en: Digital and analog form a pair: one counts steps, the other follows a continuous curve.
normal.cn: 数字与模拟成对：一个数台阶，一个沿连续曲线。

abstract.en: Picture a smooth wave sliced into a picket fence.
abstract.cn: 想象一道平滑的波被切成栅栏。

abstract.en: Picture a hand counting on its own fingers in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在黑暗里自己数着指头。

abstract.en: Picture a signature that exists only as a small row of numbers.
abstract.cn: 想象一个签名只以一小排数字存在。

examples.en: A digital copy can be duplicated without losing quality.
examples.cn: 数字副本可以无损复制。

examples.en: The museum published a digital catalogue of its drawings.
examples.cn: 博物馆发布了馆藏素描的数字目录。

examples.en: Digital records are easier to search but easier to copy.
examples.cn: 数字记录更易检索，也更易被复制。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「地（di）挤（gi）头（tal）」——手指头挤在算盘上数数，数出来的就是数字的

root: 拉丁 digitus「手指」→ digitalis「手指的」→ 英语 digital；因用手指计数，digit 引申为「数字」，digital 再引申为「用离散数值表示的」，二十世纪又扩展为「计算机技术的」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses start at the finger, move to counting, then to discrete values, computer technology, numeric displays, online media, circuits, recordings, data-only records and the contrast with analog.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从手指出发，走到计数，再到离散取值、计算机技术、数字显示、线上媒介、电路、录音、纯数据记录，以及与模拟的对立。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smooth curve cut into vertical bars whose tops join into a zigzag.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条平滑曲线被切成竖柱，柱顶连成折线。

branches.en: THE BODY: the oldest sense, still used in anatomy for fingers and toes.
branches.cn: 身体：最老的意思，解剖学里仍指手指与脚趾。

branches.en: DISCRETE WORKING: separate numbered values, and circuits that only know on and off.
branches.cn: 离散运作：分开的编号取值，以及只知开与关的电路。

branches.en: COMPUTER WORLD: machines, then the online media and markets built on them.
branches.cn: 计算机世界：先是机器，后是建立在机器上的线上媒介与市场。

branches.en: READOUT AND RECORDING: numbers shown on a clock, numbers that preserve sound and image.
branches.cn: 读数与录制：钟表上显示的数字，以及保存声音与图像的数字。

branches.en: DEMATERIALISED TRUST: signatures and money as data, defined against analog.
branches.cn: 无实体的信任：作为数据的签名与货币，在与模拟的对立中被定义。

intro.en: Digital is a Latin noun plus a Latin adjective ending, with no Greek element; later English added -ize and -ization to build the verb and noun.
intro.cn: digital 是拉丁名词加拉丁形容词词尾，不含希腊成分；后来英语加 -ize 与 -ization 构成动词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Digitus and digitalis are the only Latin pieces; the computing senses are entirely modern extensions of that pair.
latinIntro.cn: digitus 与 digitalis 是仅有的拉丁构件；计算机诸义完全是这一对词的现代延伸。

items.example: The noun names the body part used for counting.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指用来计数的身体部位。

items.example: The adjective was borrowed whole into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词被整体借入英语。

items.example: The ending makes a body part into a description.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把身体部位变成描述词。

items.example: Counting on fingers gave numerals the same name.
items.exampleCN: 用手指计数使数字获得了同一个名字。

items.meaning: of fingers; then of discrete values
items.meaningCN: 手指的；后指离散数值的
items.example: The word moved from anatomy to arithmetic to electronics.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从解剖学走到算术，再走到电子学。

items.example: Digitize means to make into digits.
items.exampleCN: digitize 意为使成为数字形式。

items.example: Digitization names the process, not one file.
items.exampleCN: digitization 指过程，不指单个文件。

items.example: The archive is stored digitally.
items.exampleCN: 档案以数字方式存储。

items.meaning: the wider move to digital ways of working
items.meaningCN: 转向数字化工作方式的更广进程
items.example: Digitalization changes how a firm works, not just its files.
items.exampleCN: digitalization 改变公司的运作方式，而不只是文件。

definition_en: the process of converting analog information into a form that a computer can store and process
core_image: 一页泛黄的纸平放在扫描台上，光线扫过，字迹变成屏幕上清晰的像素
scene: 图书室里，一页泛黄的纸平放在扫描台上，光线扫过纸面，字迹随即变成屏幕上清晰的像素。The library began the digitization of its oldest newspapers last spring.
sceneCN: 这里 digitization 指把模拟材料转换成数字形式的过程（第 1 个义项：模拟材料转成数字形式的过程）；句意：图书馆去年春天开始了最老报纸的数字化。图中可辨识物件：泛黄纸页、扫描台、光线、屏幕像素。

senses.title: Turning analog into digital form
senses.titleCN: 把模拟材料转为数字形式
senses.definition: the conversion of continuous signals, images or text into discrete numeric data
senses.definitionCN: 把连续信号、图像或文本转换成离散数字数据
senses.example: Digitization of the tape preserved audio that was already flaking.
senses.exampleCN: 磁带的数字化抢救了已在剥落的音频。
senses.why: digit plus -ization names the act of making something consist of digits, so the core sense is conversion of form.
senses.whyCN: digit 加 -ization 指使某物由数字构成的动作，核心义因此是形式的转换。

senses.title: Scanning paper documents
senses.definition: the work of capturing printed pages as images or searchable files
senses.definitionCN: 把印刷页面捕获为图像或可检索文件的工作
senses.example: Document digitization cut the storage room in half.
senses.exampleCN: 文档数字化把储藏室缩小了一半。
senses.why: offices meet the word first as scanning, because paper is the most common analog material they hold.
senses.whyCN: 办公室最先通过扫描接触到这个词，因为纸张是他们手上最常见的模拟材料。

senses.title: Converting images and sound
senses.definition: the capture of photographs, films or recordings as sampled files
senses.definitionCN: 把照片、影片或录音捕获为采样文件
senses.example: Film digitization must decide how many frames per second to keep.
senses.exampleCN: 胶片数字化必须决定每秒保留多少帧。
senses.why: each medium has its own sampling rate, but the underlying act is the same conversion of a continuous record.
senses.whyCN: 每种媒介有自己的采样率，但底层动作都是对连续记录的同一类转换。

senses.title: Encoding measurements as numbers
senses.definition: the representation of physical quantities by discrete sampled values
senses.definitionCN: 用离散采样值表示物理量
senses.example: Digitization of the sensor output loses detail between samples.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器输出的数字化会丢失采样点之间的细节。
senses.why: instruments produce continuous voltages, and digitization is what makes those voltages readable by a processor.
senses.whyCN: 仪器产出连续电压，数字化正是让这些电压能被处理器读取的步骤。

senses.title: A library or archive programme
senses.titleCN: 图书馆或档案馆的项目
senses.definition: an organized effort to convert a collection and make it accessible
senses.definitionCN: 有组织地转换一批馆藏并使其可获取的努力
senses.example: The digitization of the manuscript collection took six years.
senses.exampleCN: 手稿馆藏的数字化花了六年。
senses.why: institutions turned the technical act into a named programme with staff, standards and funders.
senses.whyCN: 机构把技术动作变成有人员、标准与资助方的具名项目。

senses.title: A step inside a wider digital shift
senses.titleCN: 更大数字化转变中的一步
senses.definition: the part of organizational change that turns existing material into data
senses.definitionCN: 组织变革中把既有材料转成数据的那一部分
senses.example: Digitization came first; new working habits came later.
senses.exampleCN: 先有数字化转换，新的工作习惯随后才来。
senses.why: consultants separate the technical conversion from the cultural change, and keep digitization for the narrower technical step.
senses.whyCN: 顾问把技术转换与文化变革分开，digitization 留给较窄的技术步骤。

senses.title: Sampling a continuous signal
senses.definition: the technical process of measuring a signal at fixed intervals and storing the values
senses.definitionCN: 按固定间隔测量信号并保存数值的技术过程
senses.example: Proper digitization requires a sampling rate above twice the highest frequency.
senses.exampleCN: 恰当的数字化要求采样率高于最高频率的两倍。
senses.why: the engineering sense is the most precise: conversion by regular sampling, with rules that decide what is lost.
senses.whyCN: 工程义最精确：按规律采样完成转换，并由规则决定丢失什么。

senses.title: Making a service paper-free
senses.definition: the conversion of forms, records and workflows into data-only processes
senses.definitionCN: 把表单、记录与流程转成纯数据流程
senses.example: Digitization of the application form removed the last queue.
senses.exampleCN: 申请表数字化取消了最后一条队伍。
senses.why: when the material is a whole service, the word describes removing paper from every step rather than scanning one page.
senses.whyCN: 当材料是整个服务时，这个词描述的是从每一步去掉纸，而不是扫描一页。

intro.en: Digitization is digit plus -ize plus -ation: a Latin noun for finger turned into a numeral, then into a verb, then into the name of a process. The computing sense is twentieth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: digitization 是 digit 加 -ize 再加 -ation：一个指手指的拉丁名词先变成数字，再变成动词，再变成过程之名。计算机义属于二十世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Digitus meant finger or toe; the word's deeper origin is uncertain, and no Latin root explains it neatly.
items.cn: digitus 指手指或脚趾；它更早的来源不确定，拉丁语里也没有哪个词根能干净地解释它。

items.en: Counting on fingers made digit the name of a numeral, and English used digit for any figure from nought to nine.
items.cn: 用手指计数使 digit 成为数字之名，英语用 digit 指零到九的任一数字。

items.en: The verb ending -ize goes back to Greek -izein through Latin -izare and French -iser; English uses it to mean make into or render.
items.cn: 动词词尾 -ize 可追到希腊语 -izein，经拉丁语 -izare 与法语 -iser 而来；英语用它表示「使成为」。

items.en: Digitize appeared in the twentieth century for converting measurements and records into numeric form, first in technical writing.
items.cn: digitize 在二十世纪出现，指把测量与记录转成数字形式，最初用于技术写作。

items.en: The noun digitization followed the verb, and libraries, archives and broadcasters made it the name of large conversion programmes.
items.cn: 名词 digitization 跟着动词出现，图书馆、档案馆与广播机构使它成为大型转换项目的名称。

items.en: The chain from digitus through the numeral, the verb ending and the noun ending is documented, with the verb ending going back to Greek -izein. The pre-Latin origin of digitus is not settled and the comparisons offered for it are reconstructions; the first dates of the computing sense are approximate.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：从 digitus 到数字义，再加动词词尾与名词词尾的链条有文献依据，动词词尾可追到希腊语 -izein；digitus 在拉丁语之前的来源尚无定论，为它提出的比较属于重构形式；计算机义的最早年代只有约数。

note.en: The first group shares the digit stem; the second group names the neighbouring processes and results, including the wider term often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组共享 digit 词干；第二组是相邻的过程与结果，包括常被混淆的更宽术语。

entries.definition: The broader adoption of digital technology across how an organization works; digitization is the narrower conversion of material into data.
entries.definitionCN: 数字技术在整个组织运作方式上的更广采用；digitization 是较窄的把材料转成数据。

entries.definition: To perform the conversion; digitization is the process or the programme built around it.
entries.definitionCN: 执行转换；digitization 是由此形成的过程或项目。

entries.definition: Of discrete numeric form; it describes the result, while digitization describes the route to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指离散数字形式；它描述结果，digitization 描述通往结果的路。

entries.definition: One numeral or one finger; it is the smallest unit the process produces.
entries.definitionCN: 一个数字或一根手指；它是这个过程产出的最小单位。

entries.definition: Capturing a page with light; it is one common method of digitization, not the whole concept.
entries.definitionCN: 用光照捕获页面；它是数字化的常见方法之一，不是整个概念。

entries.definition: Changing something from one form to another; digitization is conversion into numeric form specifically.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从一种形式变为另一种；digitization 特指转成数字形式。

entries.definition: Representing information in a defined code; digitization produces numeric samples, which may then be encoded for storage.
entries.definitionCN: 用既定编码表示信息；digitization 产出数字采样，之后可再编码存储。

entries.definition: Protecting material from loss; digitization is often done for preservation, but a digital copy is not the original object.
entries.definitionCN: 保护材料免于损毁；数字化常为保存而做，但数字副本并不等于原件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin stem, the real endings and the real programme names, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词干、真实的词尾与真实项目名，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Digit plus -ization: the ending means the process of making, so digitization is the process of making something digital.
normal.cn: digit 加 -ization：词尾意为「使……化的过程」，所以 digitization 就是使某物数字化的过程。

normal.en: The family runs digit, digital, digitize, digitization and digitalization.
normal.cn: 同族词有 digit、digital、digitize、digitization 与 digitalization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: digitization project, document digitization, digitization standard.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：数字化项目、文档数字化、数字化标准。

normal.en: Digitization is narrow, digitalization is wide: one turns paper into data, the other changes how work is done.
normal.cn: digitization 窄，digitalization 宽：一个把纸变成数据，一个改变做事方式。

normal.en: The suffix -ize came from Greek through Latin and French, so the verb looks international in every European language.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ize 经拉丁语与法语来自希腊语，所以这个动词在欧洲各语言里都显得国际化。

abstract.en: Picture a yellowed page becoming a grid of bright squares.
abstract.cn: 想象一页发黄的纸变成一格格明亮的方块。

abstract.en: Picture a sound being cut into tiny numbered slices and stacked.
abstract.cn: 想象一段声音被切成极小的编号薄片并叠起来。

abstract.en: Picture an archive losing its dust as it gains a search box.
abstract.cn: 想象一座档案馆在得到搜索框的同时失去灰尘。

examples.en: Digitization of the census returns made family history searchable.
examples.cn: 人口普查表的数字化让家族史变得可检索。

examples.en: The cost of digitization lies mostly in metadata, not in scanners.
examples.cn: 数字化的成本主要在元数据，而不在扫描仪。

examples.en: Poor digitization can preserve an image and lose the text inside it.
examples.cn: 糟糕的数字化可能保住了图像，却丢掉了里面的文字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「地（di）挤（gi）太（ta）爱（i）神（zation）」——把纸上的东西挤成数字之神，就是数字化

root: 拉丁 digitus「手指」→ digit「数字」→ 加 -ize 成 digitize「使数字化」→ 加 -ation 成 digitization「数字化过程」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the conversion from analog material to data: the general act, scanning paper, capturing media, encoding measurements, a library programme, a step in wider change, signal sampling and a paper-free service.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着「从模拟材料到数据」的转换走：一般动作、扫描纸页、捕获媒介、编码测量、图书馆项目、更大变革中的一步、信号采样，以及无纸服务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a yellowed page on a scanner, a band of light crossing it and clean pixels appearing on screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：扫描台上一页发黄的纸，一道光扫过，屏幕上出现干净的像素。

branches.en: THE ACT: continuous form turned into discrete numeric data.
branches.cn: 动作：连续形式转成离散数字数据。

branches.en: MATERIALS: paper pages, photographs, film and sound each captured by their own method.
branches.cn: 材料：纸页、照片、胶片与声音各有自己的捕获方法。

branches.en: SIGNALS: physical quantities sampled at fixed intervals, with rules about what is lost.
branches.cn: 信号：物理量按固定间隔采样，并有关于丢失什么的规则。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS: a funded programme, and one technical step inside a wider digital shift.
branches.cn: 机构：有资助的项目，以及更大数字化转变中的一步技术工作。

branches.en: SERVICES: when a whole form or service loses paper, the word describes every step.
branches.cn: 服务：当整份表单或服务去掉纸，这个词描述的是每一步。

intro.en: Digitization is Latin stem plus Greek-derived verb ending plus Latin-derived noun ending: three layers stacked in one word.
intro.cn: digitization 是拉丁词干加希腊来源动词词尾，再加拉丁来源名词词尾：一个词里叠了三层。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies digitus and the noun ending -atio; the verb ending -ize came from Greek through Latin and French before English used it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供 digitus 与名词词尾 -atio；动词词尾 -ize 在英语使用之前已经经拉丁语与法语来自希腊语。

items.example: The stem names the body part used for counting.
items.exampleCN: 词干指用来计数的身体部位。

items.example: The numeral sense came from counting on fingers.
items.exampleCN: 数字义来自用手指计数。

items.example: The ending turns a noun into a verb of making.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成「使……化」的动词。

items.example: The verb names the act performed once.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指一次完成的动作。

items.example: The ending turns the verb into the name of a process.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成过程之名。

items.example: The noun can name a whole programme.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词可以指整个项目。

items.example: The adjective describes the result of the process.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述过程的结果。

items.example: The wider term is often confused with digitization.
items.exampleCN: 这个更宽的词常与 digitization 混淆。

items.meaning: a device that performs the conversion
items.example: A digitizer turns a drawing into coordinates.
items.exampleCN: 数字化仪把图形转成坐标。

definition_zh: 使数字化；把……转成数字形式；扫描录入
definition_en: to convert analog information into digital form that a computer can store and process
core_image: 一叠旧照片被逐张放上扫描仪，边缘对齐后屏幕上出现整齐的图像文件
scene: 技术员把一叠旧照片逐张放上扫描仪，边缘对齐，屏幕上随即出现一张张整齐的图像文件。They hired students to digitize the paper archive before the roof leaked again.
sceneCN: 这里 digitize 指把纸面或模拟材料转成数字形式（第 1 个义项：把模拟信息转成数字形式）；句意：他们雇了学生来把纸面档案数字化，免得屋顶再次漏水。图中可辨识物件：旧照片、扫描仪、对齐边、屏幕文件。

pos.zh: 使数字化；转成数字形式

senses.title: To convert analog into digital
senses.definition: to turn continuous information into discrete numeric data
senses.definitionCN: 把连续信息转成离散数字数据
senses.example: The studio digitized the master tapes before they broke down.
senses.exampleCN: 工作室在母带损坏之前把它们数字化了。
senses.why: the verb means to make something consist of digits, so its core is a change of form from continuous to counted.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词意为使某物由数字构成，核心是从连续形式变为可计数的形式。

senses.title: To scan a document
senses.definition: to capture a printed page as an image or a searchable file
senses.definitionCN: 把印刷页面捕获成图像或可检索文件
senses.example: Please digitize the signed contract and send it back.
senses.exampleCN: 请把签好的合同扫描成电子件再发回来。
senses.why: paper is the analog material most people handle, so the everyday verb usually means scan.
senses.whyCN: 纸是多数人接触到的模拟材料，所以日常动词通常就是「扫描」。

senses.title: To capture images or sound
senses.definition: to record photographs, film or audio as sampled files
senses.definitionCN: 把照片、胶片或音频录成采样文件
senses.example: They digitized the oral histories and put them online.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把口述史数字化后放上网。
senses.why: each medium is a continuous record, and the verb applies wherever such a record is turned into samples.
senses.whyCN: 每种媒介都是连续记录，只要这类记录被转成采样，动词就适用。

senses.title: To encode a measurement
senses.definition: to represent a physical quantity by sampled numeric values
senses.definitionCN: 用采样数值表示物理量
senses.example: The board digitizes the voltage a thousand times a second.
senses.exampleCN: 这块板子每秒把电压数字化一千次。
senses.why: a sensor gives a continuous signal, and the verb names the step that makes it readable as numbers.
senses.whyCN: 传感器给出连续信号，动词指把它变成可读数值的那一步。

senses.title: To move a process onto digital tools
senses.titleCN: 把流程搬到数字工具上
senses.definition: to replace paper or manual steps with digital ones in a workflow
senses.definitionCN: 在工作流程中用数字步骤取代纸面或手工步骤
senses.example: The office digitized its expense claims last year.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室去年把报销流程数字化了。
senses.why: when the object is a process rather than a page, the verb means rebuilding the steps around data.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是流程而非一页纸时，动词指围绕数据重建这些步骤。

senses.title: To convert medical records
senses.definition: to turn paper charts and films into electronic patient records
senses.definitionCN: 把纸质病历与胶片转成电子病历
senses.example: The clinic digitized every chart before the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所在合并之前把每份病历都数字化了。
senses.why: hospitals hold both paper and images, and the verb covers both halves of that conversion.
senses.whyCN: 医院同时存有纸页与影像，动词涵盖这次转换的两半。

senses.title: To sample a signal
senses.definition: to measure a continuous signal at regular intervals and store the values
senses.definitionCN: 按固定间隔测量连续信号并保存数值
senses.example: The instrument digitizes the waveform at forty thousand points per second.
senses.exampleCN: 这台仪器每秒把波形数字化四万个点。
senses.why: in engineering the verb is precise: conversion by regular sampling, with a rate that decides what survives.
senses.whyCN: 在工程里这个动词很精确：按规律采样转换，采样率决定什么能留下来。

senses.title: To represent by digits
senses.definition: to express a value in numerals, in older or technical usage
senses.definitionCN: 用数字表达一个值，属较早或技术性用法
senses.example: Older manuals digitize lengths in whole millimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的手册把长度按整毫米数字化。
senses.why: before electronics, the verb could simply mean writing a quantity as digits, and that plain sense still appears in technical prose.
senses.whyCN: 在电子学之前，这个动词可以只表示把量写成数字，这一素朴义仍出现在技术文字里。

intro.en: Digitize is digit plus -ize, both parts borrowed into English: the noun from Latin digitus, the ending from Greek through Latin and French. The computing sense is twentieth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: digitize 是 digit 加 -ize，两部分都是英语借来的：名词出自拉丁语 digitus，词尾经拉丁语与法语出自希腊语。计算机义属于二十世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Digitus meant a finger or a toe; the word's deeper origin is uncertain and no Latin root accounts for it cleanly.
items.cn: digitus 指手指或脚趾；它更早的来源不确定，拉丁语里没有哪个词根能干净地解释它。

items.en: The numeral sense grew from counting on fingers: a digit became any figure from nought to nine.
items.cn: 数字义由用手指计数生长出来：一个 digit 成为零到九的任一数字。

items.en: The ending -izein made verbs of making or rendering; Latin took it as -izare, French as -iser, and English as -ize.
items.cn: 词尾 -izein 构成「使成为」的动词；拉丁语作 -izare，法语作 -iser，英语作 -ize。

items.en: The verb first meant to write a quantity as digits, a plain arithmetical sense that survives in older technical prose.
items.cn: 这个动词最初指把量写成数字，这一素朴的算术义仍活在一些较早的技术文字里。

items.en: In the twentieth century digitize shifted to the electronic conversion of signals, documents and media into machine-readable numbers.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，digitize 转为指把信号、文档与媒介电子化地转成机器可读的数字。

items.en: The stem from Latin digitus and the ending from Greek -izein are both documented. The pre-Latin origin of digitus is not settled and the comparisons offered for it are reconstructions; the first use of the verb is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：词干出自拉丁语 digitus，词尾出自希腊语 -izein，两段都有文献依据；digitus 在拉丁语之前的来源尚无定论，为它提出的比较属于重构形式；动词最早使用的年代只有约数。

note.en: The first group is the same stem in other shapes; the second group names the neighbouring actions of scanning, encoding and computerizing.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词干的其他形式；第二组是扫描、编码、计算机化等相邻动作。

entries.definition: The British spelling with -ise; the meaning and pronunciation are identical to digitize.
entries.definitionCN: 用 -ise 的英式拼写；含义与读音和 digitize 完全相同。

entries.definition: The process or programme of converting material; the verb names one act within it.
entries.definitionCN: 转换材料的过程或项目；动词指其中的一次动作。

entries.definition: The device that performs the conversion, such as a tablet or a converter.
entries.definitionCN: 执行转换的设备，如数位板或转换器。

entries.definition: Of numeric form; it describes what the object becomes after the verb is applied.
entries.definitionCN: 指数字形式；它描述动词作用之后对象的样子。

entries.definition: To capture a page or an object with light; one common way to digitize paper, but not the only one.
entries.definitionCN: 用光照捕获页面或物体；数字化纸张的常见方式之一，但不是唯一方式。

entries.definition: To express information in a defined code; digitizing produces numbers that may then be encoded for storage or transmission.
entries.definitionCN: 用既定编码表达信息；数字化产出数字，之后可再编码以存储或传输。

entries.definition: To change from one form to another; digitize is the specific conversion into numeric form.
entries.definitionCN: 从一种形式变为另一种；digitize 特指转成数字形式。

entries.definition: To put a system under computer control; it changes the system, while digitize changes the form of the material.
entries.definitionCN: 把系统交给计算机控制；它改变系统，digitize 改变材料的形态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin stem, the real verb ending and the real scanning phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词干、真实的动词词尾与真实的扫描搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Digit plus -ize: the ending means make into, so digitize means make into digits.
normal.cn: digit 加 -ize：词尾意为「使成为」，所以 digitize 就是使成为数字形式。

normal.en: The family runs digitize, digitization, digitizer, digital and digit.
normal.cn: 同族词有 digitize、digitization、digitizer、digital 与 digit。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the work: digitize a document, digitize records, digitize an archive.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出工作：数字化文档、数字化记录、数字化档案。

normal.en: The British spelling swaps -ize for -ise without changing a sound.
normal.cn: 英式拼写把 -ize 换成 -ise，读音不变。

normal.en: The oldest sense is plain: write the quantity as digits.
normal.cn: 最老的意思很素朴：把量写成数字。

abstract.en: Picture a photograph dissolving into a tray of tiny numbered tiles.
abstract.cn: 想象一张照片散成一盘带编号的小方块。

abstract.en: Picture a voice being cut into slices thin enough to stack.
abstract.cn: 想象一个声音被切成薄到可以叠起来的片。

abstract.en: Picture a paper archive walking into a screen one page at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一座纸面档案馆一次一页地走进屏幕。

examples.en: They plan to digitize the whole collection by next winter.
examples.cn: 他们计划在明年冬天之前把整个馆藏数字化。

examples.en: The device digitizes sound at a rate the ear cannot distinguish.
examples.cn: 这台设备以耳朵分辨不出的速率把声音数字化。

examples.en: Digitize the receipt before the ink fades.
examples.cn: 趁墨迹未褪，先把收据扫描成电子件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「地（di）挤（gi）太（ta）子（ze）」——把纸上的东西挤成数字的太子，就是使数字化

root: 拉丁 digitus「手指」→ digit「数字」→ 加希腊—拉丁动词词尾 -ize，构成 digitize「使数字化」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the general conversion to scanning paper, capturing media, encoding measurements, rebuilding a workflow, converting medical records, sampling signals and the older sense of writing values as digits.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般转换走到扫描纸页、捕获媒介、编码测量、重建流程、转换病历、信号采样，以及较早的「把量写成数字」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: old photographs placed one by one on a scanner, edges aligned, files appearing on screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧照片一张张放上扫描仪，边缘对齐，文件出现在屏幕上。

branches.en: THE CORE ACT: from continuous information to countable digits, and the older plain sense of writing values as numerals.
branches.cn: 核心动作：从连续信息到可计数数字，以及较早的「把量写成数字」义。

branches.en: PAPER AND CHARTS: the everyday objects offices and clinics convert first.
branches.cn: 纸页与病历：办公室与诊所最先转换的日常对象。

branches.en: MEDIA: photographs, film and oral history become sampled files.
branches.cn: 媒介：照片、胶片与口述史变成采样文件。

branches.en: SIGNALS: voltages and waveforms measured at fixed intervals by instruments.
branches.cn: 信号：仪器按固定间隔测量电压与波形。

branches.en: PROCESSES: a workflow rebuilt around data instead of paper.
branches.cn: 流程：围绕数据而非纸面重建的工作流。

intro.en: Digitize is a Latin stem with a Greek-derived verb ending, the same pattern as modernize or computerize.
intro.cn: digitize 是拉丁词干加希腊来源动词词尾，与「现代化」「计算机化」这类动词同一模式。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies digitus; the ending -ize reached English through Latin -izare and French -iser from Greek -izein.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供 digitus；词尾 -ize 由希腊语 -izein 经拉丁语 -izare 与法语 -iser 进入英语。

items.example: The stem names the counting hand.
items.exampleCN: 词干指计数的手。

items.example: The noun supplies the target form of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 名词提供动词的目标形态。

items.example: The ending turns a form into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把形式变成动作。

items.example: The verb is recorded first in technical prose.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词最早见于技术文字。

items.example: Digitization names the whole process.
items.exampleCN: digitization 指整个过程。

items.example: A digitizer is the machine, not the file.
items.exampleCN: digitizer 是机器，不是文件。

items.example: The adjective describes the finished state.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述完成后的状态。

items.example: The wider term is not a synonym.
items.exampleCN: 这个更宽的词并非同义词。

items.example: The pattern of the ending is the same.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词的词尾模式相同。

definition_zh: 电子的；电子设备的；以电子方式进行的
definition_en: relating to electrons, working by means of electronic devices, or existing as computer data
core_image: 一块绿色电路板上细密的铜线连着成排小元件，指示灯一亮一灭
scene: 桌上摆着一块绿色电路板，细密的铜线连着成排的小元件，指示灯一亮一灭。The office replaced its paper forms with electronic records last year.
sceneCN: 这里 electronic 指以计算机数据形式存在的（第 3 个义项：以电子数据形式存在的）；句意：办公室去年用电子记录取代了纸质表格。图中可辨识物件：电路板、铜线、小元件、指示灯。

senses.title: Relating to electrons
senses.definition: concerning electrons or the behaviour of charged particles in matter
senses.definitionCN: 关于电子或物质中带电粒子行为的
senses.example: Electronic charge is measured in units far smaller than a coulomb.
senses.exampleCN: 电子电荷的单位远小于一库仑。
senses.why: the adjective's root is the particle itself, so its plainest sense describes anything belonging to electron physics.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词的词根就是那个粒子，最基本的意思因此是描述属于电子物理的事物。

senses.title: Working by electronic circuits
senses.definition: describing a device that operates through valves, transistors or chips rather than mechanical parts
senses.definitionCN: 指通过电子管、晶体管或芯片而非机械部件运作的设备
senses.example: An electronic thermostat reacts faster than a wax valve.
senses.exampleCN: 电子恒温器比蜡阀反应更快。
senses.why: devices controlled by electron flow were named after that flow, and the adjective became a product category.
senses.whyCN: 由电子流控制的设备以这股电子流命名，形容词于是成了一个产品类别。

senses.title: Existing as computer data
senses.titleCN: 以计算机数据形式存在的
senses.definition: stored, sent or signed as digital data rather than on paper
senses.definitionCN: 以数字数据而非纸面形式保存、发送或签署
senses.example: Electronic records must still be readable in twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 电子记录在二十年后仍须可读。
senses.why: once records moved onto computers, the adjective marked the paperless copy of a familiar document.
senses.whyCN: 记录一旦搬到计算机上，这个形容词就标出熟悉文件的无线下纸面版本。

senses.title: Of electronic communication
senses.definition: describing messages carried by wires, radio or networks rather than by hand
senses.definitionCN: 指经线路、无线电或网络而非人手传递的消息
senses.example: Electronic mail arrived long before the web.
senses.exampleCN: 电子邮件远在万维网之前就出现了。
senses.why: communication was among the first things electronics changed, and each medium kept the adjective in its name.
senses.whyCN: 通信是电子学最早改变的事物之一，每种媒介都把形容词留在名字里。

senses.title: Produced by electronic means
senses.definition: describing music or images generated or shaped by electronic equipment
senses.definitionCN: 指由电子设备生成或塑造的音乐与图像
senses.example: Electronic music can be made without any acoustic instrument.
senses.exampleCN: 电子音乐可以不用任何原声乐器制作。
senses.why: artists adopted the adjective for work whose sound comes from circuits rather than strings or air.
senses.whyCN: 艺术家采用这个形容词，指声音来自电路而非琴弦或空气的作品。

senses.title: Of a circuit or component
senses.definition: describing the branch of engineering that deals with circuits and their components
senses.definitionCN: 指处理电路及其元件的工程分支
senses.example: Electronic design starts with the power supply.
senses.exampleCN: 电子设计从电源开始。
senses.why: engineering needed a compact label for the circuit side of electrical work, as opposed to the generation and distribution side.
senses.whyCN: 工程需要给电气工作中的电路一侧一个简短标签，以区别于发电与配电一侧。

senses.title: Of electronic warfare
senses.definition: describing military use of electromagnetic energy to detect, confuse or disable an opponent
senses.definitionCN: 指军事上利用电磁能量探测、迷惑或瘫痪对手
senses.example: Electronic warfare units jam the enemy's radios.
senses.exampleCN: 电子战部队干扰敌方的无线电。
senses.why: the military borrowed the adjective for operations fought with signals instead of shells.
senses.whyCN: 军方借这个形容词指用信号而非炮弹进行的作战。

senses.title: Of automated monitoring
senses.definition: describing tagging, tracking or surveillance carried out by electronic devices
senses.definitionCN: 指由电子设备执行的标记、追踪或监控
senses.example: Electronic tagging let the court track the defendant's movements.
senses.exampleCN: 电子标记让法庭能追踪被告的行踪。
senses.why: surveillance became automatic, and the adjective named the means by which a person or object is watched.
senses.whyCN: 监控变得自动化，这个形容词就命名了监视人或物的手段。

intro.en: Electronic is electron plus -ic. Electron was coined in 1891 from Greek ēlektron, amber, the substance that first showed electric attraction. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: electronic 是 electron 加 -ic。electron 于 1891 年由希腊语 ēlektron「琥珀」造出，琥珀是最早显示电吸引的物质。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek ēlektron meant amber. Rubbing amber and watching it attract light objects was the first known electrical effect, so the material gave its name to the force.
